ProgramName: Doctor of Business Administration in Finance
Requirements:
Submit an online application
Upload a professional resumé
Submit a 750-1,000 word statement of purpose describing your professional goals and aspirations, your previous academic preparation, and an explanation of how the DBA program fits your professional and personal aspirations.
Submit two letters of recommendation. At least one of the letters must come from a faculty member or other individual qualified to attest to your academic ability. You will submit contact information for the recommenders in the online application and they will receive instructions for submitting their letters electronically.
Submit official transcripts from all institutions of higher education attended.
An earned master’s degree in business or a related field from a regionally accredited institution, or its international equivalent, with a minimum GPA of 3.0
An earned bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution, or its international equivalent, with a minimum GPA of 3.0
Students whose native language is not English must submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores unless they have earned a degree from an accredited United States institution or from an institution in a country where English is the official language. Minimum scores required for TOEFL are 80 (internet-based), 213 (computer-based), or 550 (paper-based). The minimum IELTS score is 6.5.
Students are not required to submit GRE or GMAT scores.
Description: The Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) program at Sacred Heart University’s Jack Welch College of Business & Technology is a practitioner-oriented doctoral program designed for executives who seek to further their careers as transformational leaders, applied researchers, and university faculty. Rooted in applied research, the program allows students to delve into real-world business challenges, integrating academic theories with practical solutions. Our DBA curriculum is designed to sharpen critical thinking, analytical skills, and leadership capabilities, preparing graduates to influence decision-making at the highest levels of organizations. The program emphasizes ethical leadership and social responsibility, aligning with Sacred Heart University's mission. Graduates emerge as thought leaders, equipped to contribute to both academic scholarship and professional practice, making a significant impact in their chosen fields.
Accredidation: AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business) accreditation for the Jack Welch College of Business & Technology

ProgramName: Doctor of Education in Educational Leadership
Requirements:
Admission to the Doctor of Education in Educational Leadership program is a competitive process. Admission is based upon an applicant's academic record, professional experience, recommendations, and a personal interview with the Doctoral Admissions Committee.
Admission to the Ed.D. program requires:
*   An earned master's degree from a regionally accredited institution with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.3.
*   Evidence of five or more years of professional experience in an educational leadership role (i.e., teacher, administrator, school leader, or other leadership role).
*   Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate work submitted directly to Sacred Heart University.
*   Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant's leadership potential and/or academic ability.
*   A written statement outlining the applicant's professional goals and interest in the Ed.D. program.
*   A current resume or curriculum vitae.
*   A successful interview with the Doctoral Admissions Committee.
*   Submission of the completed online application and application fee.
Department: College of Education and Human Development
Description: The Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) in Educational Leadership program, developed and taught by accomplished practitioner-scholars, prepares educational leaders for roles in both public and private schools, higher education, and other educational and nonprofit settings. The program is committed to developing leaders who can translate current research and best practices into effective action. Designed for working professionals, the program offers flexible scheduling through a blended model of online and face-to-face instruction at our Fairfield campus. Graduates of the Ed.D. program serve as leaders, scholars, and advocates for equity and excellence. Through a focus on collaboration and social justice, graduates are equipped with a diverse set of professional skills including: research and evaluation, program and policy development, advocacy, communication, and management.

ProgramName: Doctor of Education in Higher Education Leadership
Requirements:
A master's degree in a related field from a regionally accredited institution with a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA
Official transcripts from all institutions attended
Two letters of recommendation (professional or academic)
Current resume
Statement of professional goals and objectives
No GRE required
Description: Our Doctor of Education (EdD) in Higher Education Leadership program is ideal for professionals seeking to advance into leadership and management positions in colleges and universities. The curriculum emphasizes leadership, organizational behavior, policy, finance, and assessment in higher education settings. With an EdD, you’ll become a critical analyst of higher education policy and practice, capable of leading institutions through complex changes. This program is designed for working professionals, with flexible evening and weekend classes offered at our Stamford graduate center. As an EdD in Higher Education Leadership student, you will delve into crucial topics relevant to today's evolving higher education landscape. This program is designed to provide you with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills needed to address complex challenges in higher education. You'll learn about: Leadership and Organizational Change (understanding theories of leadership, organizational behavior, and change management within higher education institutions); Higher Education Policy and Governance (analyzing the policy landscape, governance structures, and legal frameworks impacting colleges and universities); Finance and Resource Management (exploring financial models, budgeting, and resource allocation strategies specific to higher education); Assessment and Accreditation (learning about institutional effectiveness, program evaluation, and the accreditation process); Research Methods and Data Analysis (developing advanced research skills, including qualitative and quantitative methodologies, to inform data-driven decision-making); Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (examining issues of access, equity, and inclusion in higher education and developing strategies for fostering inclusive environments); and Strategic Planning and Innovation (mastering the principles of strategic planning, innovation, and entrepreneurship in higher education).

Requirements: The Department of Physical Therapy participates in the Physical Therapy Centralized Application Service (PTCAS). All applicants must apply through PTCAS. Applicants are expected to possess a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants may be admitted to the DPT program with the understanding that the undergraduate degree will be completed prior to the start of the professional phase of the program. Minimum Cumulative GPA 3.0. Minimum Science GPA 2.75. The following must be submitted to PTCAS: Completed online application to PTCAS. Official transcripts from ALL colleges and universities attended. Two letters of recommendation from professional individuals who can attest to the applicant's academic potential, communication skills, and work ethic. One letter must be from a licensed physical therapist and one from a college professor. A minimum of 50 observation hours supervised by a licensed Physical Therapist. These hours can be paid or volunteer, in a minimum of two different settings. All applicants must submit official GRE scores directly from ETS to PTCAS (Sacred Heart University Code: 0746). The GRE must be taken within five years of the application. A CV or Resume is required from all applicants. A personal statement, one page in length, addressing the following: Why are you interested in pursuing a career in physical therapy? Why have you selected Sacred Heart University's DPT program? Additional requirements apply for international applicants, including TOEFL scores, WES evaluation, and financial certification.
Description: The Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) program at Sacred Heart University is a rigorous, post-baccalaureate, entry-level professional program designed to prepare students for the practice of physical therapy. The DPT program is a full-time, three-year program consisting of a sequential plan of study that includes classroom, laboratory, and clinical coursework. The program is specifically designed to meet the academic and clinical requirements for students to be eligible for licensure examinations in all 50 states and the District of Columbia. Physical therapists are health care professionals who help patients reduce pain and improve or restore mobility. They treat patients of all ages who have injuries, disabilities, or other health conditions. The comprehensive program prepares students as generalist physical therapy practitioners, while emphasizing a commitment to community service, global engagement, and professional development. The curriculum integrates basic sciences, clinical sciences, and research to prepare graduates for contemporary physical therapy practice. The program’s learning environment stresses critical thinking, problem-solving, and evidence-based practice across the lifespan. The Doctor of Physical Therapy program at Sacred Heart University is committed to providing outstanding education, compassionate service, and rigorous scholarship within an interprofessional environment dedicated to improving health outcomes.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Physical Therapy program at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE), 3030 Potomac Ave., Suite 100, Alexandria, Virginia 22305-3085; telephone: 703-706-3245; email: accreditation@apta.org; website: http://www.capteonline.org. If needing to contact the program/institution directly, please call 203-371-7788 or email dpt@sacredheart.edu. The program is undergoing a review for re-accreditation that will conclude in 2023.

ProgramName: Family Nurse Practitioner Doctor of Nursing Practice
Requirements: Master of Science in Nursing from an accredited institution. Minimum GPA of 3.2 on a 4.0 scale. Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. Current, unencumbered RN license from the state in which the student plans to complete clinical hours. Current national certification as an Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (APRN). Evidence of successful completion of a graduate-level statistics course. Two letters of recommendation from professional colleagues/supervisors who can attest to the applicant’s academic and clinical abilities. Current curriculum vitae or résumé. Statement of professional goals. Interview with a faculty member.
Description: The DNP is a terminal practice degree that prepares advanced practice nurses for leadership roles in healthcare. Sacred Heart University offers a DNP with several concentrations. The program is designed to prepare graduates to translate research into practice, lead quality improvement initiatives, and impact healthcare policy. The curriculum emphasizes evidence-based practice, patient safety, health informatics, and interprofessional collaboration. Students will engage in scholarly activities, including the completion of a DNP project, which addresses a clinical problem or health system issue. The DNP program is offered in both full-time and part-time formats. The Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP) concentration within the DNP program prepares registered nurses to provide comprehensive primary healthcare to individuals and and families across the lifespan. FNPs assess, diagnose, treat, and manage acute and chronic illnesses, focusing on health promotion, disease prevention, and patient education. Graduates are eligible for national certification as a Family Nurse Practitioner and state licensure.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) program at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE), 655 K Street NW, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001, 202-887-6791.

ProgramName: Ph.D. in Organization Development, Change & Effectiveness
Requirements:
Applicants for admission to the Ph.D. in Organization Development, Change & Effectiveness program must possess a master's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must submit the following materials:
*   Online application
*   Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework
*   Current resume or curriculum vitae
*   Three letters of recommendation submitted by former professors or supervisors
*   A personal statement of at least 750 words describing professional experiences, reasons for pursuing a Ph.D. in ODCE, and career aspirations following completion of the degree
*   A research statement of 500 words or less addressing a current issue in organization development, change, or effectiveness. The statement should articulate a research question that could be explored in the Ph.D. program.
*   Official scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) or Graduate Management Admissions Test (GMAT) must be submitted unless the applicant has received a master’s degree from Sacred Heart University and maintained a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA. The GRE/GMAT must have been taken within the last five years.
*   All international students from non-English speaking countries must submit official scores from the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS).
Description: Sacred Heart University’s Ph.D. in Organization Development, Change & Effectiveness (ODCE) prepares leaders to transform organizations and communities through theory and practice. The doctoral program prepares scholar-practitioners who apply critical inquiry, ethical decision-making, and organizational theory to design and implement transformational change. Students develop knowledge and skills to lead complex change processes, evaluate organizational interventions, and contribute to the body of knowledge in ODCE. This program is for working professionals with a minimum of a master’s degree and at least five years of professional work experience. Students are prepared for careers in internal and external consulting, human resources, organizational leadership, and academia. The ODCE Ph.D. is a cohort model where students work together from admission to graduation and develop professional networks and friendships. Courses are delivered in a hybrid format, with monthly residencies meeting in person on the Sacred Heart University campus. Students complete their studies with a research-based dissertation.

Requirements: The Social Work Ph.D. program will accept applications on a rolling basis. Admission requires a master’s degree in social work from a CSWE-accredited program, with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale). The following documents must be submitted to complete your application: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended; Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to your academic abilities and readiness for doctoral study. At least one of these letters must be from an academic source; Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV); Personal statement detailing your academic and professional goals, research interests, and why you are interested in pursuing a Ph.D. in Social Work at Sacred Heart University (minimum 750 words); Master’s degree writing sample (e.g., thesis, research paper, scholarly paper, journal article, etc.) that demonstrates your capacity for scholarly writing; Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required; A copy of your current social work license (LCSW preferred); Non-native English speakers must submit a Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS) score. A minimum TOEFL score of 80 (internet-based) or IELTS score of 6.5 is required.
Description: Our online Ph.D. in Social Work program is designed for social work professionals who want to develop the advanced research and practice skills needed to make a meaningful impact in the field. This unique program provides an opportunity for students to advance their knowledge and prepare for leadership roles in social work education, administration, practice, and research. With a focus on social justice and human rights, students in our Ph.D. in Social Work program engage in rigorous scholarship, critical thinking, and ethical decision-making. Through advanced coursework, research projects, and dissertation, students will gain the expertise to address complex social problems and contribute to the advancement of social work knowledge. The curriculum is delivered in an online, interactive format, allowing working professionals to balance their studies with their personal and professional commitments.

Requirements:
Completed online graduate application (including the non-refundable application fee)
Official transcripts of all college-level work (undergraduate and graduate) sent directly from the issuing institution(s). If accepted, official final transcripts noting degree conferral are required prior to matriculation.
Minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
Official transcripts verifying a Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) degree with an overall GPA of 3.25 on a 4.0 scale from a nationally accredited program. The Post-Master's DNP requires a non-clinical MSN.
Current, active, unencumbered RN license(s) from the state(s) in which clinical practice will occur and current, active, unencumbered advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) license(s), if applicable.
Professional Resume or Curriculum Vitae
Personal Statement/Essay that speaks to your professional goals and how the DNP will help you achieve them (1-2 pages)
Two letters of recommendation (one from a supervisor/employer and one from an academician is preferred)
Interview with a College of Nursing faculty member
Evidence of completed 500 clinical hours at the graduate level
Copy of BLS/ACLS/PALS certification(s) per specialty
Description:
The Post-Master’s DNP is designed for master’s-prepared advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs) seeking to advance their knowledge and skills in evidence-based practice, leadership, and health care policy. It is a doctoral-level program to prepare the APRN at the highest level of clinical nursing practice. The program focuses on providing advanced knowledge in nursing science, theory, and research, as well as developing advanced competencies in evidence-based practice, organizational leadership, and health care systems. Graduates of the program are prepared to lead complex health care systems, translate research into practice, and improve population health outcomes. Coursework for the DNP program builds upon master’s level coursework in the areas of: Nurse Anesthesia, Family Nurse Practitioner, Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner, Clinical Nurse Leader.
The DNP curriculum is based on the AACN’s Essentials of Doctoral Education for Advanced Practice.
For more information, please visit the Sacred Heart University College of Nursing website.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) program is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Athletic Training
Requirements: Baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited institution, or international equivalent. Undergraduate cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Completion of prerequisite coursework (Anatomy and Physiology I with lab, Anatomy and Physiology II with lab, Biology with lab, Chemistry with lab, Physics with lab, Statistics, General Psychology, and Medical Terminology). Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Two letters of recommendation from faculty members, supervisors, or athletic training professionals. Resume or curriculum vitae. Personal statement addressing the applicant’s interest in the athletic training profession and desire to attend Sacred Heart University. Official scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) general test are NOT required. Demonstration of 50 hours of observation under the direct supervision of a BOC-certified athletic trainer. The observation hours can be in any setting (e.g., high school, college/university, clinic, professional sport, industrial). These hours must be verified by the supervising athletic trainer(s). International applicants must provide evidence of English language proficiency through official TOEFL or IELTS scores unless they have completed a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution where English is the language of instruction. Official scores must be submitted directly to the Sacred Heart University Office of Graduate Admissions.
Description: The Sacred Heart University Master of Science in Athletic Training (MSAT) is an entry-level professional program designed for students with a bachelor’s degree in a related field who are seeking to become certified athletic trainers. The program prepares students to become highly competent, compassionate, and ethical healthcare professionals capable of providing patient-centered care in a variety of clinical settings. The curriculum emphasizes evidence-based practice, critical thinking, and interprofessional collaboration, providing students with the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to excel in the dynamic field of athletic training.
Accredidation: The Master of Science in Athletic Training program at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Athletic Training Education (CAATE), 2001 K Street NW, Third Floor North, Washington, DC 20006. The program has been placed on Probation as of February 24, 2023, by the CAATE. For more information, please see the CAATE's Public Disclosure Statement.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Clinical Mental Health Counseling
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Sacred Heart University MA in Clinical Mental Health Counseling program, you must hold a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution and a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA. While a background in psychology or a related field is helpful, it is not required for admission. Candidates must provide: Completed Application Form, Resume, Personal Statement, Official Transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities, Two Letters of Recommendation, Interview.
Description: The CACREP-accredited online MA in Clinical Mental Health Counseling program at Sacred Heart University prepares students for careers as licensed professional counselors (LPCs). In as few as three years, you can learn to assess, diagnose, and treat clients from diverse backgrounds in a wide variety of settings. Through comprehensive coursework, hands-on practicum and internship experiences, and faculty mentorship, you will develop the clinical skills and knowledge needed to help individuals, families, and groups achieve optimal mental health and well-being. Upon graduation, you will be eligible for licensure in many states, though requirements may vary by state. This program also fulfills the educational requirements for students interested in pursuing the Marriage and Family Therapy (MFT) credential.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Film & Television Production
Requirements: Applicants for the Master of Arts in Film & Television Production are required to submit the following: A completed application, A non-refundable application fee, Official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, including proof of bachelor's degree earned with an undergraduate GPA of at least 3.0. Two letters of recommendation from faculty or employers. A statement of purpose (500–1,000 words). A resume of professional and/or volunteer experience in the industry or other related fields. A writing sample of at least 5 pages, which can include creative writing (e.g., screenplay, short story, theatrical play) or analytical/critical writing (e.g., academic paper, critical essay, film analysis).
Description: The Master of Arts in Film & Television Production program is a cutting-edge, hands-on master’s degree designed for students who want to develop creative content for screens of all sizes, from web to television to theatrical release. In today’s rapidly evolving media landscape, the roles of writer, producer, director, and editor are often combined. Our program emphasizes storytelling across all platforms and provides students with skills in critical analysis, visual storytelling, writing for the screen, producing, directing, cinematography, editing, and post-production. The program offers students the opportunity to choose between a thesis or a capstone project. Upon completion, students will have a portfolio of work ready for the job market. Full-time and part-time options are available. The program can be completed in two years of full-time study.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Higher Education & Student Affairs
Requirements: All applicants for the Master of Arts in Higher Education & Student Affairs must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution and meet the general requirements for admission to graduate studies at Sacred Heart University. In addition, applicants for the Master of Arts in Higher Education & Student Affairs must submit the following: Official transcripts of all previous college work. There are no specific prerequisite courses required for admission to the program.
Department: College of Education and Human Development
Description: The Master of Arts in Higher Education & Student Affairs (MA-HESA) program at Sacred Heart University prepares students to serve in administrative and leadership roles within higher education settings. Students are trained to work effectively with diverse college students in areas such as student activities, residential life, career development, student leadership, admissions, and advising. This 36-credit program prepares students to become reflective practitioners by integrating theory, research, and practice in their chosen professional areas. The program emphasizes self-reflection, social justice, inclusion, ethical practices, and the development of effective leadership skills. Through classroom learning, fieldwork, and internships, students are prepared to be collaborative and innovative leaders and managers in higher education. The program is offered in a hybrid format.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Sports Communication and Media
Requirements: Completed online graduate application: A non-refundable application fee is required. The fee is waived for Sacred Heart University alumni. Official transcripts: From all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution and have a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. Applicants with an undergraduate GPA below 3.0 may be considered for conditional admission. Two letters of recommendation: From supervisors, professors, or others who can speak to the applicant’s professional or academic capabilities. (Required) Graduate Record Examination (GRE): The GRE is not required for admission. (Not Required) International applicants: Additional requirements include an official English translation of all academic records and official scores from the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS). A minimum TOEFL score of 80 (Internet-based) or IELTS score of 6.5 is required. International applicants must also provide evidence of adequate financial resources.
Description: The Master of Arts in Sports Communication & Media program at Sacred Heart University is a dynamic and innovative graduate program designed to equip students with the advanced knowledge and practical skills necessary to thrive in the rapidly evolving sports communication industry. This program provides an in-depth exploration of the theoretical, ethical, and strategic dimensions of sports media, preparing graduates for leadership roles in various facets of the field. The Mission of the Master of Arts in Sports Communication & Media program is to develop agile and ethically-minded professionals who possess a comprehensive understanding of the evolving sports communication landscape. Through a blend of theoretical foundations and practical applications, the program aims to cultivate critical thinking, effective communication, and media production skills, empowering graduates to create impactful narratives, manage complex communication challenges, and contribute meaningfully to the sports industry.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Strategic Communications and Public Relations
Description: The Sacred Heart University Master of Arts in Strategic Communication and Public Relations program provides a comprehensive graduate education for those seeking leadership roles in a wide range of communication fields. Through a curriculum that emphasizes both theoretical understanding and practical application, students develop advanced skills in strategic planning, public relations, media relations, digital communication, crisis management, and persuasive messaging. The program is designed for current communication professionals seeking to advance their careers, as well as recent graduates looking to enter the dynamic world of strategic communication. Graduates emerge with a sophisticated understanding of the evolving media landscape and the ability to craft compelling narratives that resonate across diverse platforms. The program fosters critical thinking, ethical decision-making, and a global perspective essential for effective communication leadership in today's complex environment.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Teaching Music
Requirements: Admission to the M.A.T. program requires evidence of outstanding academic success and strong recommendations. Applicants must also complete the Sacred Heart University graduate application. Required documents include: Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate work completed. An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale is required. Transcripts from outside the U.S. require a credential evaluation. Two letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or professional work. Statement of purpose (500–1,000 words) describing the applicant’s interest in the field, career goals, and reasons for applying to the graduate program. A current résumé. Official GRE scores (if undergraduate GPA is below 3.0). Sacred Heart University's GRE code is 3780. Additional requirements for M.A.T. in Teaching Music: Audition and interview. A portfolio with recent examples of the applicant’s work may also be requested.
Description: The Master of Arts in Teaching (M.A.T.) is designed for college graduates who seek initial certification to teach at the elementary or secondary school levels. The M.A.T. program provides candidates with a solid theoretical and practical background in education. Through fieldwork and extensive clinical practice experiences, candidates learn to integrate theory and research with current best practices to become reflective practitioners who understand the diverse needs of students in public and private schools. The Music (PK-12) certification area is designed for individuals who hold an undergraduate degree in Music.
Accredidation: The M.A.T. program in the Isabelle Farrington College of Education and Human Development has been awarded accreditation by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) for a period of seven years, from Fall 2021 to Fall 2028.

Requirements: Applicants must have a Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with a minimum GPA of 2.75. Required documents include official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities, a professional resume, two letters of recommendation, and a Statement of Purpose. International students must submit English proficiency test scores (TOEFL/IELTS). GMAT/GRE scores are recommended but not mandatory. Applicants need to complete an online application and pay the application fee.
Concentration: Finance, Marketing, Human Resources, Business Analytics
Description: The Sacred Heart University Master of Business Administration (MBA) program builds on your previous academic and professional experiences to transform you into an effective leader. With a strong emphasis on ethical decision-making, global awareness, and innovative problem-solving, the SHU MBA prepares you for success in today's dynamic business environment. Our rigorous curriculum, experienced faculty, and strong industry connections ensure you gain the knowledge, skills, and network needed to advance your career. The program offers a variety of specializations, including Finance, Marketing, Human Resources, and Business Analytics, allowing students to tailor their MBA to their career goals. Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of international business practices and challenges and cultivate strong ethical decision-making skills crucial for responsible leadership.
Accredidation: The Jack Welch College of Business & Technology at Sacred Heart University is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Film and Television Production
Description: The MFA in Film & Television at Sacred Heart University is an intensive, two-year, terminal degree program that trains students in the art and craft of visual storytelling. Students select a primary area of focus among the following: Producing, Directing, Screenwriting or Cinematography. The program emphasizes narrative fiction, creative collaboration, critical thinking, and independent filmmaking with a focus on preparing graduates for success in the entertainment industry. Students will receive extensive instruction in both theory and practice in the fields of film and television, with additional study in the critical, aesthetic, and historical aspects of these media. Throughout the program, students work in both individual and group settings to write, direct, and produce films of increasing complexity that culminate in a thesis film that meets professional standards. Students are given the opportunity to present their work at film festivals and industry showcases. Sacred Heart University’s MFA in Film & Television prepares graduates for careers as independent filmmakers, as well as for work in a variety of capacities in the professional film and television industries.

Requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
*   Possess a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution.
*   Demonstrate academic ability for graduate study as evidenced by your academic record.
*   Have a minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale).
*   Have completed undergraduate coursework in statistics and microeconomics or their equivalents (e.g., AP Economics, AP Statistics). If you have not taken these courses, you must successfully complete them by the time of enrollment.
*   Have at least two years of full-time post-baccalaureate experience in a health care setting or a related field (e.g., direct patient care, hospital administration, public health, health tech, health consulting, life sciences, biotech, pharma).
*   International applicants have additional requirements detailed on the International Applicants page.

Application Components:
*   Online Application
*   Transcripts
*   Letters of Recommendation (3 required)
*   Statement of Purpose (Required)
*   Resume or CV (Required)
*   Supplemental Questions (Required)
*   GRE (Optional)
*   TOEFL/IELTS (If applicable)
Description: The Master of Health Administration (MHA) program at Sacred Heart University is a 36-credit online or on-ground program designed for healthcare professionals seeking to advance their careers in leadership and management roles within the rapidly evolving healthcare industry. Our MHA program prepares you for executive-level positions in hospitals, health systems, long-term care facilities, consulting firms, pharmaceutical companies, and state and federal agencies. Upon completion of the MHA program, graduates will be able to: Master healthcare-specific management theories and practices; Exhibit leadership skills and competencies for various healthcare settings; Apply ethical principles to professional practice and decision-making; Analyze data and evidence for informed decision-making in healthcare administration; Articulate effective communication strategies for diverse healthcare stakeholders; Evaluate the impact of healthcare policy and regulations on organizations. Students will learn about: Healthcare Systems & Policy; Healthcare Finance; Strategic Management in Healthcare; Healthcare Law & Ethics; Quality Improvement in Healthcare; Health Informatics; Leadership in Healthcare Organizations; Research Methods in Health Administration.
Accredidation: Sacred Heart University is accredited by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE).

Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Physician Assistant Studies Program requires a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must apply to the PA Program through the Central Application Service for Physician Assistants (CASPA) at caspaonline.org. The application cycle opens in April annually. The deadline for CASPA application is September 1. It is recommended that applicants submit their applications early.

Minimum GPA requirements:
*   Cumulative GPA of 3.0
*   Science GPA of 3.0
*   A minimum of a “C” (2.0) is required for all prerequisite courses.

Prerequisite Courses (A minimum of “C” is required for all courses. All science courses must be for science majors.)

*   Biology with lab (2 semesters/8 credits)
*   Chemistry with lab (2 semesters/8 credits)
*   Anatomy & Physiology with lab (2 semesters/8 credits) (within 5 years of application)
*   Microbiology with lab (1 semester/4 credits)
*   Statistics (1 semester/3 credits)
*   Biochemistry or Organic Chemistry with lab (1 semester/4 credits)
*   Medical Terminology (1 semester/1 credit)

Other Admission Requirements:

*   Graduate Record Examination (GRE): General Test is required. The SHU code for the GRE is 3780.
*   Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation are required. Letters should be from individuals who can attest to the applicant’s academic preparedness, professional experience, and personal qualities for a career as a PA (e.g., professor, academic advisor, supervisor). It is recommended that at least one letter be from a practicing physician assistant or other healthcare provider with whom the applicant has worked directly.
*   Shadowing/Healthcare Experience: A minimum of 500 hours of direct patient care experience is required. Shadowing a PA is highly recommended.
*   International Applicants: Please refer to the Graduate International Admissions webpage for additional requirements.
*   Immunizations: All accepted applicants will be required to meet SHU's immunization requirements prior to matriculation. Details will be provided upon acceptance.
*   Background Check/Drug Screen: All accepted applicants will be required to successfully complete a criminal background check and drug screen prior to matriculation. Details will be provided upon acceptance.
*   Interview: Qualified applicants will be invited for an on-campus interview.
Description: The Master of Physician Assistant Studies (MPAS) Program at Sacred Heart University is an intensive 27-month, full-time program designed to prepare graduates to provide comprehensive health care services to diverse populations in a variety of clinical settings. The curriculum is delivered in a cohort model and designed to integrate a strong basic science foundation with clinical medicine. The program includes both didactic and supervised clinical practice experiences (SCPEs). Throughout the didactic year, students acquire the medical knowledge and clinical skills necessary to provide patient care within a medical team. During the clinical year, students participate in required and elective rotations designed to develop competence in primary care and medical and surgical specialties. The curriculum also emphasizes interprofessional collaboration, evidence-based medicine, patient advocacy, medical ethics, and cultural sensitivity to prepare students for the contemporary healthcare environment. Upon graduation, students are eligible to sit for the Physician Assistant National Certifying Examination (PANCE), administered by the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA). Completion of the program does not guarantee certification or state licensure.
Accredidation: The ARC-PA has granted Accreditation-Continued status to the Sacred Heart University Physician Assistant Program sponsored by Sacred Heart University. Accreditation-Continued is an accreditation status granted when a currently accredited program is in compliance with the ARC-PA Standards. Accreditation remains in effect until the program closes or withdraws from the accreditation process or until accreditation is withdrawn for failure to comply with the Standards. The approximate date for the next comprehensive review for the Sacred Heart University Program sponsored by Sacred Heart University will be March 2032. The review date is contingent upon continued compliance with the Accreditation Standards and ARC-PA policy. The program’s accreditation history can be viewed on the ARC-PA website at http://www.arc-pa.org/accreditation-history-sacred-heart-university/.

Description: The Master of Science in Accounting program is designed for individuals who have already earned a bachelor’s degree in accounting or a related field and wish to deepen their knowledge, enhance their professional skills, and prepare for the Uniform Certified Public Accountant (CPA) Examination. The program’s curriculum provides students with advanced knowledge in financial accounting, auditing, taxation, and business law, emphasizing ethical considerations and critical thinking. The program also offers students the opportunity to develop skills in data analytics and financial modeling, which are increasingly important in the accounting profession. Upon completion of the program, graduates will be well-prepared for a variety of careers in public accounting, corporate accounting, government, and not-for-profit organizations. They will also be eligible to sit for the CPA Examination in Connecticut and other states, depending on their prior academic background and work experience. Application for admission
Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. All international transcripts must be evaluated by a NACES accredited service.
Resume/CV
Two letters of recommendation from a professor or work supervisor (Required for applicants with an undergraduate GPA below 3.0).

Description:
Sacred Heart University’s Master of Science in Business Analytics & Applied AI program is for the intellectually curious who want to explore big data and uncover insights to solve complex business problems. Our STEM-designated master’s program will prepare you for a range of exciting careers in industries experiencing rapid growth.
Our Master of Science in Business Analytics & Applied AI (MSBA&AI) program prepares you for the critical role of data analyst, data scientist, business intelligence analyst, and more in a world increasingly driven by data. The program teaches you to apply theoretical principles, analytical methods and problem-solving techniques to big data, and how to communicate results and inferences effectively to stakeholders. You’ll learn to collect, clean, manipulate, visualize, and analyze data to find the insights that matter most. You’ll become proficient in using state-of-the-art tools and technologies such as Python, R, SAS, SQL, and Tableau, and will develop expertise in statistical modeling, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and deep learning. This STEM-designated master’s program offers small classes with an average student-to-faculty ratio of 13:1, allowing for personalized attention and mentorship from experienced faculty who bring real-world industry experience to the classroom. You'll also benefit from networking opportunities and career development support.
Accredidation: Sacred Heart University’s Jack Welch College of Business & Technology is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. AACSB accreditation is the hallmark of excellence in business education, earned by less than five percent of the world’s business programs.

Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to graduate study at Sacred Heart University. In addition, applicants should submit the following to the Office of Graduate Admissions: Completed online application, Official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, A cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (applicants with a GPA of 2.75-2.99 may be admitted on a provisional basis), Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to the applicant's academic potential for graduate study, A statement of professional goals (500-word essay), Official GRE scores (verbal, quantitative, and analytical writing sections) are encouraged but not required. For applicants with a GPA below 3.0, official GRE scores are required.
Description: The Master of Science in Chemistry program provides advanced education in chemistry with options to pursue either a thesis-based or non-thesis-based degree. Students in the program develop skills in critical thinking, problem-solving, and scientific communication as they gain deep knowledge of advanced topics in chemistry. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for a wide variety of careers in industry, government, and academia, or for further graduate study in Ph.D. programs in chemistry or related fields. The program is designed to meet the needs of recent graduates with a Bachelor of Science degree in chemistry, professional chemists seeking to enhance their knowledge, and high school chemistry teachers seeking to advance their careers. The Master of Science in Chemistry program has 30 credits.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Science and Information Technologies

Requirements: Applicants must possess a bachelor’s degree in computer science or a related discipline from an accredited institution. Applicants who do not hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science or a closely related field may be required to complete preparatory coursework prior to being admitted to the program. In addition to the general requirements for admission to graduate studies at Sacred Heart University, applicants for the Master of Science in Cybersecurity program must also submit: Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, a statement of professional goals, a current resume, two letters of recommendation.
Description: The Master of Science in Cybersecurity program prepares students for leadership positions in the area of network and computer security, in both government and private industry. The curriculum provides both breadth and depth in areas of network and computer security, and in related areas such as network forensics and applied cryptography. Students will develop the theoretical background and practical experience necessary to plan, design, implement, and audit secure computing infrastructures.

Description: The Master of Science in Digital Marketing program prepares students with the expertise needed to plan, develop, and implement digital marketing strategies. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of current trends, tools, and platforms in digital marketing, including search engine optimization (SEO), social media marketing, content marketing, email marketing, mobile marketing, analytics, and digital advertising. ProgramName: Master of Science in Finance and Investment Management
Requirements:
Admission to the MS in Finance & Investment Management program is open to applicants who hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Consideration for admission will be given to candidates who show academic promise and professional potential based on the following criteria:

Description: The Master of Science in Finance and Investment Management (MSFIM) program prepares students for leadership positions in financial services. It is designed for recent college graduates and for professionals working in finance or other fields who wish to advance or change their careers. The MSFIM program provides a rigorous, cutting-edge education in all areas of finance, including corporate finance, financial markets and institutions, investment management, and financial risk management. Students learn how to analyze complex financial problems and develop innovative solutions. The program prepares students for professional certifications, including the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA®) designation.
Accredidation: The Jack Welch College of Business & Technology at Sacred Heart University is one of the fewer than five percent of business schools worldwide accredited by AACSB International – the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Healthcare Informatics
Requirements: Admission to the Master of Science in Healthcare Informatics program at Sacred Heart University is granted to applicants who hold a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution with a GPA of 3.0 or better. All application materials, including official transcripts, personal statement, and two letters of recommendation, are submitted through our online portal. The GRE is waived for applicants with an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher.
Description: The Master of Science in Healthcare Informatics program at Sacred Heart University is designed for working professionals and recent graduates from a variety of backgrounds who want to make a difference in the healthcare field. In this program, you will develop the knowledge and skills necessary to improve patient care outcomes and reduce costs using information technology and analytics. Healthcare informatics bridges the gap between clinical practice, information technology, and business, applying principles from all three to improve healthcare services and delivery. Our rigorous, relevant curriculum covers crucial topics in the field, including healthcare data analytics, project management, health information systems, health data security, and interoperability. Courses combine online learning with an intensive, immersive residency experience at the end of the program, which takes place on Sacred Heart's campus. Our faculty bring real-world experience to the classroom, ensuring that you graduate with practical, in-demand skills. Upon graduation, our program will prepare you to make an impact in a variety of healthcare settings. Learning Outcomes include: Analyze existing healthcare processes and identify opportunities for informatics interventions; Evaluate, design, and implement informatics solutions to improve patient outcomes, reduce costs, and enhance the efficiency of healthcare delivery; Lead and manage informatics projects, ensuring their successful integration into healthcare systems; Apply ethical and legal principles to the management and use of health information, ensuring patient privacy and data security; Communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, bridging the gap between clinical, technical, and administrative teams; Utilize advanced data analytics techniques to interpret complex healthcare data and inform decision-making. Graduates of the MS in Healthcare Informatics program at Sacred Heart University are prepared for leadership roles in a variety of healthcare settings, including hospitals, clinics, government agencies, and technology companies. Potential career paths include: Clinical Informatics Specialist, Health Data Analyst, Project Manager, Healthcare IT Consultant, Chief Medical Information Officer (CMIO), Chief Nursing Information Officer (CNIO).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Industrial/Organizational Psychology
Requirements:
A completed online application
Official undergraduate transcripts showing an earned bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. An undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher is preferred. If your undergraduate degree is not in psychology, you may be conditionally admitted and required to complete additional courses.
A current resume

Two letters of recommendation from academic or professional references

Application Fee
International applicants: please see specific requirements for international students.
Description:
Industrial/Organizational Psychology is the scientific study of working and the application of that science to workplace issues facing individuals, teams, and organizations. The I/O Psychology program at Sacred Heart University provides students with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary to address such issues, including how to select and recruit employees, how to measure and improve job performance, and how to foster employee motivation, satisfaction, and well-being. The curriculum also focuses on the systematic application of psychological principles and research methods to improve decision-making and performance in organizations.

Students will graduate with a strong theoretical and practical understanding of Industrial/Organizational Psychology, prepared to work as consultants or organizational leaders in business, healthcare, government, or non-profit organizations. The program also offers students the opportunity to gain applied experience through various internships, research, and consulting projects that help foster students’ professional network and career development.

Requirements: Applicants for admission to the Master of Science in Nursing must: Hold a current, active, unencumbered RN license in at least one state in the U.S. Have earned a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) degree from an accredited institution. Have a minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Submit a completed application and nonrefundable fee. Submit official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate work. Submit a personal statement describing their goals for graduate study and for their professional career. Submit two letters of recommendation from professional or academic sources familiar with the applicant’s skills and abilities. Successfully complete an admission interview with a faculty member. Concentration: Nurse Educator, Nursing Management & Executive Leadership, Clinical Nurse Leader (CNL), Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP), Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP), Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP)
Description:
The Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) program at Sacred Heart University prepares nurses to advance their careers and to provide leadership in professional nursing. The program is designed for registered nurses with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) or an Associate’s degree in Nursing (ADN) who desire to broaden their knowledge, skills, and values. This program builds upon a baccalaureate degree in nursing or an associate degree. The MSN program prepares graduates for advanced nursing practice roles as clinical nurse leaders, nurse educators, or nurse practitioners in primary care, acute care or psychiatric mental health settings. MSN program goals include preparation of graduates to:
* Provide evidence-based, patient-centered care and promote the health of individuals, families, groups, and communities across diverse settings and across the continuum of care.
* Assume leadership roles in designing, managing, and evaluating health care delivery systems.
* Integrate information, technology, and advanced knowledge to improve quality and safety in health care.
* Engage in the systematic inquiry and application of research to nursing practice.
* Analyze organizational and health policy for the improvement of nursing and health care.
* Engage in collaborative practice with healthcare professionals to improve client outcomes.
* Integrate ethical principles in advanced nursing practice.

Students who complete the MSN program may choose to pursue a doctoral degree in nursing.
Accredidation: The Sacred Heart University College of Nursing BSN, MSN, DNP and Post-Graduate APRN Certificate Programs are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Nursing Administration
Master of Science in Occupational Therapy
Requirements: Applicants must complete an online application for the Master of Science in Occupational Therapy (MSOT) via OTCAS (Occupational Therapy Centralized Application Service). All applicants must meet the following general admission requirements: Baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Completion of prerequisite courses with a grade of B or better in each science course, and a minimum grade of C+ in all other prerequisite courses. These prerequisite courses include: Anatomy & Physiology I with Lab (4 credits), Anatomy & Physiology II with Lab (4 credits), General Psychology (3 credits), Developmental Psychology or Child/Adolescent Development (3 credits), Abnormal Psychology (3 credits), Sociology or Anthropology (3 credits), Statistics (3 credits), and Medical Terminology (1 credit - online course acceptable). Graduate Record Exam (GRE) scores within the last five years are strongly recommended but not required. Two letters of reference are required; one reference must be from a professor who can speak to academic ability, and the second reference can be from a second professor, an academic advisor, or a supervisor (paid or volunteer). Submission of a current resume or curriculum vitae, including all professional, volunteer, and observation experiences. A personal essay on the topic 'Why I wish to pursue a career in occupational therapy'. A minimum of 40 hours of observation in at least two different occupational therapy practice settings, under the supervision of a licensed occupational therapist (experience must be documented on a verification form). Selected applicants may be invited for an on-campus interview.
Description:
The Sacred Heart University Master of Science in Occupational Therapy program has a rich history of educating occupational therapists for more than 20 years, beginning as an entry-level master’s degree program, transitioning to a clinical doctoral program (OTD) in 2013 and now returning to the entry-level Master of Science degree (MSOT). The mission of the program is to educate competent and compassionate occupational therapists who are leaders, scholars, and innovators who serve the community through ethical and evidence-based practice across diverse settings. This mission is aligned with the vision of the University, College of Health Professions, and Department of Occupational Therapy.

The program is designed as a hybrid-model curriculum, integrating online coursework with face-to-face sessions and fieldwork experiences. This model allows for flexibility for the working student while ensuring a strong foundation in occupational therapy theory and practice. The curriculum emphasizes occupation-based, client-centered, and evidence-based practice to prepare graduates to work with individuals, groups, and populations across the lifespan in a variety of traditional and emerging practice settings. Students will engage in active learning through a variety of modalities, including case studies, simulations, projects, and collaborative discussions. The program culminates in a capstone experience where students apply their knowledge and skills to address a real-world occupational therapy challenge. Upon successful completion of the MSOT program, graduates will be eligible to sit for the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) examination.
Accredidation: The Master of Science in Occupational Therapy program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) of the American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA), located at 6116 Executive Boulevard, Suite 200, North Bethesda, MD 20852-4929. ACOTE’s telephone number c/o AOTA is (301) 652-AOTA and its Web address is www.acoteonline.org. Graduates of the program will be eligible to sit for the national certification examination for the Occupational Therapist administered by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT). After successful completion of this exam, the individual will be an Occupational Therapist, Registered (OTR). In addition, all states require licensure in order to practice; however, state licenses are usually based on the results of the NBCOT Certification Examination. Note that a felony conviction may affect a graduate’s ability to sit for the NBCOT exam or to attain state licensure.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Speech-Language Pathology
Requirements: A completed graduate application form. A non-refundable application fee. Official transcripts from all institutions attended documenting an earned bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited college or university, demonstrating a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. A bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution, preferably in communication sciences and disorders (CSD). Applicants who do not have a CSD degree must complete the undergraduate pre-requisite course sequence prior to matriculation. GRE general test scores are required for all applicants. Three letters of recommendation. A written essay regarding interest in the SLP profession. Résumé. Evidence of 25 hours of observation of a licensed SLP. A personal interview may be required. For international applicants, a TOEFL/IELTS score is required if English is not the applicant’s primary language.
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) program in Speech-Language Pathology at Sacred Heart University provides students with the academic and clinical foundations required for a professional career as a speech-language pathologist. The program is designed to fulfill the academic and clinical requirements for the Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC) in Speech-Language Pathology awarded by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA), for state licensure in Connecticut, and for the Connecticut Department of Education endorsement. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical and evidence-based clinical practices across the life span. Students acquire knowledge and skills in the prevention, assessment, and treatment of speech, language, swallowing, and hearing disorders in diverse populations. The program offers opportunities for graduate students to develop expertise in specialized areas through clinical placements in Sacred Heart University’s on-campus clinic, area hospitals, public schools, and private practices.
Accredidation: The Master of Science (M.S.) education program in Speech-Language Pathology at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, 2200 Research Boulevard #310, Rockville, MD 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700.
ScholarshipType: Graduate Assistantships, Departmental Scholarships, Endowed Scholarships

ProgramName: Master of Science in Strategic Human Resource Management
Requirements:
Application Checklist for Graduate Admissions
To apply for Sacred Heart University's Master of Science in Strategic Human Resources Management program, you must submit the following:
*   A completed online application
*   A non-refundable application fee
*   Official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. Official transcripts must be sent directly from the issuing institution(s). If you have attended an international institution, a World Education Services (WES) credential evaluation is required.
*   A current resume
*   Two letters of recommendation (professional or academic)
*   A 750-1,000 word personal statement addressing your career goals and how the Master of Science in Strategic Human Resources Management will help you achieve those goals.
*   The GMAT/GRE is waived for applicants with a minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 from an accredited institution. Applicants with a cumulative undergraduate GPA of less than 3.0 are required to submit GMAT or GRE scores. GMAT/GRE waivers are also available for applicants who have five or more years of professional work experience and hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
*   International applicants must submit a TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test score report unless the applicant has received a degree from an accredited institution in the United States or from a country where English is the official language.

Additional Requirements:
*   An on-campus or virtual interview may be required.
*   Admission to the Master of Science in Strategic Human Resources Management is competitive, and meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee admission.
Description:
A master’s degree in Human Resource Management from Sacred Heart University prepares you to be a leader in the fast-paced, competitive world of business. Our Master of Science in Strategic Human Resource Management (MS in SHRM) emphasizes the strategic importance of human resources in organizations, and offers you a cutting-edge curriculum in organizational theory, data analytics, labor relations, employment law, talent acquisition, total rewards, and organizational development. Our program will provide you with the necessary skills and knowledge to address the contemporary challenges faced by global organizations today, helping you to lead their human resource function through data-driven decisions.
Sacred Heart University’s MS in SHRM curriculum is specifically aligned with the Society for Human Resource Management’s (SHRM) HR Curriculum Guidebook and Templates. This means that students who graduate from the MS in SHRM program are fully prepared to take either the SHRM-CP or SHRM-SCP certification exam.
The MS in SHRM can be completed on a full-time or part-time basis. Full-time students can complete the program in two years. Students have the option to pursue the degree completely online or in a hybrid format, which includes a blend of online and evening on-campus classes at our Fairfield, CT campus.
SHRM is the world's largest HR professional society. SHRM-certified professionals are recognized as experts and leaders in the HR field, and they are critical to the success of their organizations. Sacred Heart University's MS in SHRM prepares you to become an industry leader and to successfully obtain professional certification.
Accredidation: Sacred Heart University's Welch College of Business & Technology is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Curriculum and Instruction
Requirements: Online graduate application; Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities. Transcripts must include proof of a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited institution with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale); Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant's academic ability and/or professional experience (e.g., professor, employer, supervisor); Personal statement: A one- to two-page essay describing the applicant's professional goals, qualifications for graduate study, and reasons for pursuing the MA in Curriculum and Instruction; Resume outlining professional experience, educational background, and any relevant accomplishments; A copy of a valid teaching certificate or a statement describing intent to seek a teaching certificate (if applicable). Applicants may be granted conditional admission without a teaching certificate provided they meet all other admission requirements; International students must also submit: Official TOEFL or IELTS scores (a minimum score of 80 IBT for TOEFL or 6.5 for IELTS is required). International students may be exempt from this requirement if they have earned a degree from a U.S. institution; Credential evaluation of foreign transcripts (WES or ECE evaluation).
Department: College of Education and Human Development
Description: Our Master of Arts in Curriculum & Instruction degree is designed to serve licensed elementary and secondary school teachers who wish to enhance their professional knowledge in curriculum development, instructional design, and assessment. This program is for teachers who want to deepen their understanding of research and apply it to improve student learning in their classrooms and schools. It is also designed for teachers seeking a more prominent role in school leadership. At Sacred Heart, you will find a collaborative and supportive environment, where you can acquire new skills and knowledge to address today’s most pressing educational challenges.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Special Education
Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Arts in Special Education program requires the following:
*   Official transcripts of all prior undergraduate and graduate coursework
*   Minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale
*   Two letters of recommendation from individuals able to assess the applicant’s academic and professional abilities
*   A written statement of professional goals

Description: The Master of Arts in Special Education (MASE) program at Sacred Heart University is designed for both certified general educators seeking to earn their initial certification in special education, and those already certified in special education interested in advanced study in the field. The program provides the knowledge, skills, and dispositions necessary to meet the needs of individuals with disabilities in elementary, middle, and high school. The program emphasizes the use of evidence-based instructional strategies, assistive technology, and collaboration with families and other professionals. Graduates of the program are prepared to assume leadership roles in special education and advocate for individuals with disabilities.

ProgramName: Advanced Graduate Certificate in Nursing Education

Admission to the Advanced Graduate Certificate in Nursing Education program requires a completed online application (including application fee) and the following documents:

Description: The Advanced Graduate Certificate in Nursing Education provides registered nurses with the knowledge and skills necessary to assume the role of nurse educator in academic and/or clinical settings. Graduates are prepared to meet the needs of diverse learners and to address the challenges in contemporary nursing education. This program offers advanced education for nurses holding a master’s degree in nursing. With the increased demand for doctorally prepared nursing faculty, the Nursing Education Post-Master’s Certificate has been designed to assist nurses with their doctoral studies. This certificate program is open to nurses who hold a master's degree in nursing and who are either currently enrolled in a nursing doctoral program (PhD or DNP) or are planning to enroll in a nursing doctoral program. The 12-credit certificate offers foundational education in advanced pedagogy for nurses who are seeking to be effective educators in a variety of settings. The certificate is awarded upon successful completion of the coursework. The individual wishing to pursue the advanced graduate certificate must satisfy the requirements for admission to graduate study in nursing at Sacred Heart University.

ProgramName: Advanced Graduate Certificate in Nursing Management and Executive Leadership
Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to graduate programs at Sacred Heart University, as published in the graduate catalog. In addition, applicants for the Post Master’s Certificate in Nursing Management and Executive Leadership must have: A master’s degree in nursing from an accredited program. Graduate cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale. Current unencumbered RN license in the state in which they practice. Submission of current curriculum vitae (CV). Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate programs.
Description: This advanced graduate certificate is designed for nurses with a master’s or doctoral degree in nursing to enhance knowledge and skills in nursing management and executive leadership. Nurses will be prepared to assume a variety of management and executive roles in diverse health care organizations. The program focuses on critical management skills such as financial management, human resource management, and strategic planning, as well as executive leadership skills to promote excellence in nursing care delivery.

Requirements: Applicants to the Business Analytics Certificate program must satisfy the following requirements: A bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited college or university. Official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Two letters of recommendation. A professional resume. A personal statement. All international students must submit a TOEFL/IELTS/PTE score. If the applicant has received a bachelor's or master's degree from a college or university where English is the language of instruction (as recognized by Sacred Heart University), the TOEFL/IELTS/PTE is waived.
Description: The Business Analytics Certificate provides students with the fundamental knowledge and skills needed to understand, interpret, and apply modern analytical techniques to support decision-making processes across various business functions. Graduates will learn to use analytical and statistical tools to describe, predict, and prescribe solutions for complex business problems. The program integrates data analysis, statistical modeling, and business intelligence to provide a comprehensive understanding of how data-driven insights can be leveraged for strategic advantage. The certificate is suitable for professionals seeking to enhance their analytical capabilities or those looking to pivot into data-centric roles within the business world.

ProgramName: Certificate of Advanced Study in Play Therapy
Requirements:
Applicants must possess a master's degree in Counseling, School Psychology, Social Work, Marriage & Family Therapy, Special Education, or a related mental health field. All applicants must hold a license or be license-eligible in Connecticut or their state of residence. Applications for admission are reviewed by the Program Director. Minimum requirements include:
* Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended
* Two letters of recommendation from professional sources addressing academic capability, clinical aptitude, and readiness for post-graduate training
* Resume or CV
* Statement of professional goals (essay)
* If applicable, copies of certifications and/or licenses
Department: College of Health and Human Services
Description:
The Certificate of Advanced Study (CAS) in Play Therapy is designed for master’s level clinicians who seek to gain specialized knowledge and skills in play therapy. The CAS meets the educational requirements for the Registered Play Therapist™ (RPT™) and Supervisor (RPT-S™) credentials through the Association for Play Therapy (APT). The CAS is designed to facilitate the professional growth and development of students, preparing them to work effectively with children, adolescents, and families across diverse settings. The program also prepares clinicians for a variety of leadership positions within the field of play therapy.
Students completing the CAS in Play Therapy will be able to:
* Apply advanced knowledge of play therapy theories, techniques, and interventions to address the needs of diverse populations.
* Demonstrate ethical and culturally sensitive practice in play therapy, adhering to professional standards and guidelines.
* Integrate theoretical knowledge with practical skills to effectively assess, diagnose, and treat clients using play-based approaches.
* Utilize research and evidence-based practices to inform clinical decision-making in play therapy.
* Develop a strong professional identity as a play therapist, committed to lifelong learning and professional development.
Accredidation: Meets the educational requirements for the Registered Play Therapist™ (RPT™) and Supervisor (RPT-S™) credentials through the Association for Play Therapy (APT).

ProgramName: Sixth-Year Degree in SEAL for Social Justice Leadership
Department: Isabelle Farrington College of Education and Human Development
Description: This 30-credit Sixth-Year Degree program (Educational Leadership and Administration concentration) is designed for educators who have earned a Master’s degree and seek advanced preparation as leaders and social justice advocates in schools, districts, higher education, community organizations, and other educational settings. This program is for educators who want to enhance their leadership skills, develop advanced competencies in social-emotional learning, and advocate for more equitable educational environments. This program provides students with the opportunity to explore critical topics in educational leadership, social justice, and social-emotional learning. Graduates of the program will be prepared to assume leadership positions in various educational and community settings. Students will develop skills in the following areas: leading for social justice, fostering positive school cultures, creating inclusive learning environments, promoting social-emotional learning, implementing evidence-based practices, and advocating for equitable policies and practices. Through coursework, field experiences, and a capstone project, students will engage in deep inquiry into the challenges facing education and develop innovative solutions to promote social justice and equity. The program integrates the fields of educational leadership, social-emotional learning, and social justice. This combination offers a distinctive approach to preparing leaders who can drive positive change and create more inclusive and equitable educational systems.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships, Graduate assistantships, Institutional scholarships
