Through hands-on projects, state-of-the-art laboratories, and experiential learning opportunities, students gain real-world skills and prepare for successful careers in a wide range of engineering fields. Our dedicated faculty, with extensive industry experience, provide personalized mentorship and guidance, ensuring students receive a high-quality education and develop the problem-solving and critical thinking skills essential for success.

Requirements: Official High School Transcript, Recommendation Letter (from a teacher or counselor), SAT/ACT Scores (Optional for Fall 2024 applicants), Common Application or SHU Application (including essay).
Description: Sacred Heart University’s Bachelor of Arts in English offers an engaging and inspiring curriculum that prepares you to thrive in a wide range of professions. Our program focuses on developing students' critical reading and thinking skills, sharpening their ability to analyze and interpret complex texts, and empowering them to articulate their ideas with clarity and precision through effective writing. The English major also fosters creativity, cultural awareness, and a deep appreciation for the power of storytelling. Graduates are equipped with highly transferable skills sought after by employers in various fields, including education, publishing, journalism, marketing, law, and non-profit work.

The English minor is a natural for anyone who loves literature and writing, and it also complements any major by strengthening skills in analysis, communication, and critical thinking. It offers a wonderful opportunity to develop a deep appreciation for language, culture, and human experience, and it provides a strong foundation for a variety of career paths.

Requirements: Current SHU students interested in declaring an Environmental Studies minor should contact Dr. Valerie LaMotte at lamottev@sacredheart.edu.
Description: Climate change, pollution, renewable energy, species extinction, and global warming: these are complex challenges requiring interdisciplinary approaches. Sacred Heart University's Environmental Studies Minor prepares students to address critical environmental issues through coursework in a variety of disciplines and a required internship or research project. Students who pursue the minor often go on to careers in environmental law, urban planning, environmental education, public health, advocacy, sustainable business, conservation, journalism, and more. A minor in Environmental Studies helps students develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills, and a commitment to civic engagement and social justice. These qualities are sought by employers in a range of fields, as well as by graduate programs.

Requirements: This minor is open to all Sacred Heart University students. Students must have an overall GPA of 2.0 or higher to declare this minor.
Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
Description: Sacred Heart University’s minor in Esports Management will give you the skills you need to become an industry leader. Learn about the business of esports—including its events, teams, leagues, and digital content. The minor provides a strong foundation in a rapidly growing, billion-dollar industry. The minor is offered to all undergraduate students.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Exercise Science -
Requirements: To be considered for admission as a first-year student, you will need to submit the following: Complete and submit the Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application; An official high school transcript listing all courses taken and grades received through the end of the junior year; One recommendation letter from your high school counselor; One recommendation letter from a high school teacher; SAT/ACT Scores (Optional); Application Essay (Optional).
Concentration: Pre-Athletic Training, Pre-Physical Therapy, Strength and Conditioning
Description:
Sacred Heart University's Exercise Science program is nationally recognized as one of the best in the Northeast. Our undergraduate curriculum prepares students for careers in fields such as clinical exercise physiology, strength and conditioning, sports performance, and corporate wellness. Graduates of our program are also well-prepared for graduate study in exercise science, athletic training, physical therapy, physician assistant studies, and occupational therapy.
As an exercise science major, you will study human movement and how the body responds to exercise. You’ll also learn how to use exercise to prevent and treat chronic diseases and injuries, and to improve human health and performance. Our Exercise Science program is designed for students who are passionate about exercise, health, and wellness.
In addition to our general Exercise Science program, you can choose to specialize in one of three areas: Pre-Athletic Training, Pre-Physical Therapy, or Strength and Conditioning. All of our students gain valuable hands-on experience in the classroom, in the lab, and in internships with a wide variety of clinical and sports organizations. You will complete a required minimum of 400 hours of internship experiences as part of the curriculum.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Diocesan, Phi Theta Kappa, Transfer Student

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Fashion Marketing & Merchandising -
Requirements: Required materials for freshmen applicants: Common Application, Official high school transcripts, Official scores from the SAT or ACT (Sacred Heart University is a test-optional institution. See our test-optional policy for more information.), A letter of recommendation from your counselor or a teacher, Personal Essay (this is part of the Common Application), Mid-year senior grades (if applying ED, EA, or Priority).
Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
Description: Do you envision a career in the dynamic world of fashion? Sacred Heart University's Bachelor of Science in Fashion Marketing and Merchandising prepares you to work in this exciting global industry. Rooted in a strong business core curriculum, this cross-disciplinary program focuses on both the creative and quantitative aspects of fashion. You will learn about consumer behavior, product development, global sourcing, retail operations, marketing strategies and trend forecasting. Our program provides students with real-world experiences through partnerships with companies like Bloomingdale’s, Macy’s, J.C. Penney, Saks Fifth Avenue, Rent the Runway, Tommy Hilfiger, Marc Jacobs, Ralph Lauren, Vineyard Vines, Vineyard Brands, Chanel, Elie Tahari, and Diane von Furstenberg. With a variety of career paths to choose from, our graduates have gone on to become retail buyers, merchandise planners, visual merchandisers, product developers, fashion event coordinators, fashion forecasters, public relations specialists, stylists and more. Many of our graduates pursue careers in areas such as digital marketing, social media and entrepreneurship. You’ll be prepared for success in the ever-evolving business of fashion.
ScholarshipType: Academic Scholarships, Presidential Scholarship, Honors Program Scholarship, Performing Arts Scholarships, Athletic Scholarships, Need-Based Financial Aid

Requirements: Official high school transcript(s), One letter of recommendation (school counselor or teacher), Essay or personal statement (submitted with Common App or SHU App)
Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
Description:
Finance is the science of money management. Our bachelor of science in finance provides you with a foundation in the analytical tools and quantitative methods necessary to become a successful financial professional. If you want to pursue a career in corporate finance, investment management, or financial planning, our finance program is for you. Learn about:
* Financial statements
* Financial forecasting
* Investment analysis
* Portfolio management
* Risk management
* Options and futures markets
* International financial management
* Financial modeling
You will gain a strong understanding of how financial markets function. Our rigorous curriculum combined with faculty who bring real-world experience to the classroom will help you achieve your career goals. Through an integrated capstone course and the opportunity to pursue research projects, you will learn to apply financial theory to practical applications. We also offer a student-managed investment fund where students actively manage a portion of the University’s endowment portfolio.
As a graduate of our finance program, you will be prepared for a wide range of jobs in various financial fields, including:
* Investment banking
* Commercial banking
* Corporate finance
* Personal financial planning
* Portfolio management
* Risk management
* Real estate
* Insurance
You will also be well-positioned to pursue advanced graduate studies or professional certifications such as the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA).
ScholarshipType: Academic Scholarships, Performing Arts Scholarships, Athletic Scholarships, Scholarships for Transfer Students, Endowed and Restricted Scholarships

Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
ScholarshipType: Academic Merit, Catholic High School, Transfer, Music, Performing Arts, SHU Legacy, Campus Ministry, Phi Theta Kappa, Athletic

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Financial Technology (FinTech) -
Requirements: Official High School Transcript, Counselor Recommendation, Essay (minimum 250 words on a topic of your choice; you may select one of the Common Application essay prompts or write about another topic that is important to you), $50 non-refundable application fee (waived if you apply online). SAT/ACT scores are optional under a test-optional policy for Fall 2024 freshman applicants.
Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
Description:
Sacred Heart University’s Bachelor of Science (BS) in Financial Technology (FinTech) is a cutting-edge program designed to equip students with the skills and knowledge needed to thrive in the rapidly evolving financial services industry. FinTech integrates finance with technology, focusing on innovative solutions to traditional financial challenges. Our program provides a comprehensive understanding of financial markets, products, and services, combined with proficiency in the technological tools and techniques that are reshaping the industry.

Students will delve into topics such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, data analytics, cybersecurity, and algorithmic trading, learning how these technologies are applied in banking, investment management, insurance, and other financial sectors. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience, practical application, and ethical considerations, preparing graduates for careers in FinTech startups, established financial institutions, regulatory bodies, and technology companies.

Our BS in FinTech program is interdisciplinary, drawing expertise from the Welch College of Business & Technology. Students will gain a strong foundation in both financial principles and technological advancements, fostering a holistic understanding of the FinTech ecosystem. Graduates will be prepared to innovate, lead, and adapt in a dynamic global financial landscape, contributing to the development and implementation of future financial solutions.
Accredidation: The Welch College of Business & Technology is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Transfer Student, Performing Arts, Alumni & Family

Description: French minor students are exposed to the languages and cultures of the Francophone world while developing a wide range of critical thinking and communication skills necessary to become global citizens. While the study of French opens the door to numerous career paths, it also complements other majors like business, education, communication, political science, international affairs, hospitality, and allied health. In addition to a comprehensive curriculum, students have many opportunities to explore French and Francophone culture through study abroad programs, the French club, and campus events. The French minor also gives students a competitive edge for prestigious Fulbright Scholarships and other international programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Game Design & Development -
Requirements: Online Application (Sacred Heart University application or the Common Application), Official High School Transcript from all high schools attended, SAT or ACT Scores (See 'Test-Optional Policy' below), Essay: Required by Sacred Heart University if applying via the SHU Application; for the Common Application, the essay is part of the application, Letter of Recommendation from a school counselor or teacher.
Description: The game design and development bachelor's degree program at Sacred Heart University challenges students to develop the next generation of games, apps and interactive technologies for education, entertainment and other applications. Students learn how to create engaging experiences that solve real-world problems. They explore the entire game design and development lifecycle, from conceptualization and prototyping to coding and launch. The bachelor's degree in game design and development provides a practical, project-based curriculum that prepares graduates for careers in game design, game development, mobile app development, interactive media and more. Students build a strong portfolio of projects throughout the program, culminating in a senior capstone project where they develop and launch their own game or interactive application.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Performing Arts, ROTC, Transfer

Description: The Geriatric Health Care minor offers undergraduate students of all majors the opportunity to obtain the education needed to effectively serve the older adult population. This minor is open to all students regardless of major but is especially useful for students in the areas of nursing, physical therapy, occupational therapy, social work, exercise science, physician assistant studies and other health-related fields. Through hands-on experience and fieldwork, students will gain valuable skills to address the complex needs of older adults.

The Global Health minor focuses on key global health issues, challenges, and solutions. This interdisciplinary minor allows students from all academic areas to gain knowledge about the health issues that transcend national boundaries and are influenced by circumstances or experiences in other countries. The minor focuses on prevention, treatment, and care for those with existing conditions, as well as the study of inequities in health and healthcare. The goal is to provide students with a greater understanding of what impacts global health, as well as the policies and initiatives that affect the health of populations worldwide. The minor is a useful addition for students interested in careers in public health, humanitarian aid, medicine, social work, nursing, government, and policy. It also serves as preparation for graduate school programs related to public health and global studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Studies -
Requirements: All applicants must submit: A completed Common Application, Official high school transcript, School Counselor Recommendation, and an essay or personal statement. Official SAT or ACT scores are optional. Optional submissions include: Teacher Recommendation, Résumé, and Portfolio.
Description: The Global Studies program provides students with the intellectual tools to understand the complexity of our increasingly interconnected world. You will explore current events, social and cultural issues, economic trends, political systems, and historical contexts that transcend national borders. The program emphasizes an interdisciplinary approach, drawing from various fields such as history, political science, sociology, economics, and anthropology. Students develop critical thinking, research, and communication skills essential for navigating global challenges and opportunities. Graduates are prepared for careers in international organizations, government agencies, non-profits, multinational corporations, and graduate studies in fields such as international relations, public policy, and global affairs.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Performing Arts, Athletic, ROTC, Need-based

Description: The minor in global studies provides students with a multidisciplinary approach to understanding the world. Students in the minor will have the opportunity to engage with various disciplines, including history, political science, sociology, economics, business, languages, and cultures, to develop a comprehensive understanding of global issues. Students pursuing the minor will gain a global perspective while learning about other cultures and critically analyzing the increasingly interconnected world. The global studies minor is an interdisciplinary program that draws on courses from various departments. This minor provides a foundational understanding of global issues while offering flexibility for students to tailor their studies based on their interests. The minor will provide students with a deeper understanding of global issues, cross-cultural competencies, and the ability to engage effectively in a globalized world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Graphic Design -
Requirements: Completed Application (Common App or Sacred Heart University Application), Official high school transcripts, SAT or ACT scores (optional), One letter of recommendation (from a school counselor or teacher), Essay. A successful applicant will have a strong college preparatory curriculum, including four years of English, three years of math, two to three years of science, two to three years of social studies, and two years of the same foreign language.
Description: Graphic design is a diverse and multifaceted discipline, and at Sacred Heart University, we’ll help you develop the skills and understanding needed to thrive in this exciting field. Our Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Graphic Design offers a comprehensive curriculum that emphasizes conceptual problem-solving, aesthetic sensibility, technical proficiency and professional practices. Through a combination of traditional and digital media, you’ll learn to communicate effectively across various platforms, including print, web and interactive media. Our faculty are experienced professionals who are dedicated to providing a dynamic and supportive learning environment. You'll gain hands-on experience through studio projects, internships and collaborations, preparing you for a successful career in graphic design or further graduate studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Science -
Requirements: A completed application (Common Application or SHU Online Application). An official high school transcript, including senior year courses in progress. Official SAT/ACT test scores (see Test Optional Policy below). A letter of recommendation from your school counselor or a teacher. An essay or personal statement (required for Common Application, optional for SHU Application). Official college transcript(s) if applicable.
Description: Sacred Heart University’s Bachelor of Science in Health Science prepares students for a wide range of careers in healthcare, including allied health, healthcare administration, public health, health and wellness, and health education. With an emphasis on prevention, wellness, and evidence-based practice, students gain a deep understanding of health determinants, health promotion strategies, and healthcare delivery systems. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills, preparing graduates to address the complex challenges facing healthcare today. The Health Science major provides a strong foundation for various careers in the healthcare industry and for graduate studies in allied health fields, such as physical therapy, occupational therapy, athletic training, physician assistant, and public health. You will learn how to promote wellness, prevent disease, and improve health outcomes in diverse populations. Our curriculum focuses on health promotion, disease prevention, health education, and leadership, equipping you with the skills to make a meaningful impact in the lives of others.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Athletic, Performing Arts, Special Interest Programs

Requirements: Completed Application for Admission (including Sacred Heart-specific questions), Official High School Transcript(s). Optional: Test Scores (SAT/ACT) — Sacred Heart University is test-optional. Optional: Letter of Recommendation. Optional: Essay. Optional: Activities List. Interview (by invitation).
Description:
Historians seek to understand the human experience through the careful study and critical analysis of the past. The study of history helps students develop an understanding of themselves and their world, as well as an appreciation for the diversity of human experience. The skills students develop in history courses – critical thinking, research, and writing – are highly valued in both academic and professional fields.
Our faculty are dedicated to providing students with an excellent education that prepares them for a wide range of careers and graduate studies. The department offers a wide range of courses, covering diverse historical periods and geographical regions, including American, European, Latin American, African, and Asian history. In addition to traditional lecture courses, students have opportunities to engage in experiential learning through internships, research projects, and study abroad programs.
The History Department provides students with a solid liberal arts foundation and the skills necessary for success in a rapidly changing world. A history major provides excellent preparation for law school, graduate school, education, journalism, public history, government, business, and non-profit organizations.
Students can also pursue a minor in history.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Endowed & Restricted, Outside

Requirements: First-year applicants should submit the following: Official High School Transcript(s); One letter of recommendation (academic recommended); College Essay (See Common App prompts); Optional: SAT/ACT Scores (see test optional policy). A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) is recommended. Sacred Heart University will complete an holistic review of all applications. This review will consider high school academic performance, including your cumulative GPA, academic rigor and course selection, an essay (required for some programs, recommended for others), and letters of recommendation (optional).
Description: The History Minor at Sacred Heart University offers students from all majors the opportunity to cultivate a deeper understanding of the past. Through a diverse range of courses, students will explore different historical periods and regions, developing critical thinking, research, and analytical skills essential for success in various professional fields and graduate studies.

The Honors Minor provides highly motivated and high-achieving Sacred Heart University students from any major with an opportunity to enhance their academic experience through advanced research, interdisciplinary courses, and special extracurricular programming. Students apply for admission to the Honors Minor in the spring of their freshman year. The curriculum builds on previous learning and intellectual curiosity with the goal of fostering lifelong learners who are engaged citizens in a global society. Students in the Honors Minor benefit from: Opportunities for advanced research and interdisciplinary coursework. Special extracurricular programming. Mentorship from faculty committed to honors education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Hospitality, Resort and Tourism Management -
Requirements:
At Sacred Heart University, we welcome ambitious and talented students who are prepared to be challenged academically and inspired to achieve more than they ever thought possible. Sacred Heart has a holistic application review process, which means that we consider every part of your application. Our admissions team considers your academic performance in high school, counselor recommendation, extracurricular activities, and demonstrated interest in Sacred Heart. While not required for admission, we recommend submitting a personal essay. You may apply through the Common Application or the SHU Application portal.
First-Year Application Requirements:
* Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application
* Official High School Transcript(s)
* Official College Transcript(s) (If Applicable)
* SAT/ACT Scores (Optional - Sacred Heart University is test-optional)
* Recommendation Letter (One counselor recommendation is required. An additional letter from a teacher is optional and encouraged.)
* Personal Essay (Optional)
Department: Isabelle Farrington College of Education & Human Development
Description: The Hospitality, Resort and Tourism Management program provides students with the academic foundation for career opportunities and growth in all areas of the hospitality, resort, and tourism industry. This multi-billion dollar industry is the largest and fastest growing industry in the world, with management opportunities for graduates in hotels, resorts, country clubs, spas, cruise lines, airlines, tour companies, theme parks, attractions, entertainment, gaming, retail, restaurants, catering, private clubs, and meeting and event planning. Graduates of the program will be uniquely prepared for the demands of the 21st century global market. The curriculum provides a strong business core coupled with specialized courses that address the unique management needs of the hospitality and tourism industry. The program requires 120 credit hours for graduation and includes a required internship in an approved setting. The program is offered in the Welch College of Business & Technology. Students pursuing a B.S. in hospitality, resort, and tourism management may not also earn a B.S. in business administration.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Athletic, Performing Arts, University Endowed, Phi Theta Kappa

Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
Description: The Human Resource Management minor is designed to develop students’ knowledge and skills in human resource management functions as well as general management practices. Students will understand the major HR areas including staffing, compensation, training and development, and employee relations. The minor aims to enhance students’ understanding of the strategic role of HR in achieving organizational success and effective human capital management practices. The Human Resource Management minor is an excellent complement to most majors in the Welch College of Business & Technology, as well as several other colleges at Sacred Heart University. This minor is not available to Human Resource Management majors.

Requirements: A completed application (Common Application or SHU Application), Official high school transcripts, Official SAT or ACT scores (optional for Fall 2024, 2025, 2026, and 2027 applicants), A letter of recommendation from your school counselor or teacher, An essay or personal statement.
Description: Illustrators are creative communicators whose work is critical to telling stories across a variety of media — from books, magazines, and newspapers to comics, advertising, and animation. Sacred Heart University’s Bachelor of Arts in Illustration teaches students a broad range of drawing, painting, and digital techniques while helping them develop their own unique visual voice. You'll learn how to develop concepts, create compelling narratives, and master the tools of the trade to prepare for a successful career as a professional illustrator. In the Illustration BA program, students develop a strong understanding of foundational art principles and build advanced skills in areas such as: Drawing and painting techniques; Digital illustration software and tools; Visual storytelling and narrative development; Character design and concept art; Editorial illustration; Book illustration; Sequential art; Branding and advertising illustration; Professional practices for illustrators.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies -
Requirements: One completed Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application, official high school transcript(s) from all high schools attended, one guidance counselor recommendation, and one essay.
Description: If you have diverse interests and want to create a unique course of study, Sacred Heart’s interdisciplinary studies program may be the perfect fit. You will design your own major by combining three distinct, yet related, areas of study from across the University. Guided by a faculty advisor, you'll craft a personalized curriculum that aligns with your passions and career aspirations. This flexible program emphasizes critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication, preparing you for a wide range of professions and graduate studies. Interdisciplinary studies allows students to create an academic plan that explores three academic disciplines from across the University. This self-designed curriculum is perfect for students with diverse interests and career goals. Working closely with a faculty advisor, students select three areas of focus and develop a unique course of study. The program emphasizes critical thinking, research, and communication skills, preparing graduates for a variety of careers and graduate school.
ScholarshipPercentage: 99% of first-time, full-time undergraduate students receive financial aid.

Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
Description: International Business helps students explore the global economic, political, and social issues that affect business. Students pursuing this minor will gain a better understanding of how business is conducted on a global scale. This minor is open to all Sacred Heart University students.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Athletic, Need-based, Departmental, ROTC, Outside Scholarships

Description: The Irish Studies minor provides students with the opportunity to examine the complexity of Irish culture through the study of literature, history, religion, and the arts. Drawing on the expertise of faculty across the College of Arts and Sciences, the minor combines courses offered in multiple departments to give students an interdisciplinary understanding of Ireland past and present. Students interested in the minor should contact the English Department Chair, Dr. Margaret Moss, for more information.
ScholarshipType: Academic, Athletic, Performing Arts, Need-Based, Institutional Grants

Description: Sacred Heart University’s Italian minor will help you learn to speak, read, and write Italian and provide you with a deeper understanding of Italian history and culture. You can use your minor in conjunction with any major and apply it to a variety of careers in the humanities, international relations, business, education, and social sciences. You will gain a global perspective and develop analytical and critical thinking skills, preparing you for a variety of roles in the global marketplace. Whether you study abroad in Italy or take courses on campus, you will learn from expert faculty and immerse yourself in the Italian language and culture.

Requirements: To apply for admission to Sacred Heart University, first-year applicants must submit the following: Common Application, Official High School Transcript(s), SAT and/or ACT scores (optional for most programs), School Counselor Recommendation, Essay or Personal Statement. The essay on your Common Application satisfies this requirement.
Description: The Sacred Heart University Bachelor of Arts in Journalism program combines the strengths of a liberal arts education with hands-on experience in various media. Through courses in writing, reporting, editing, video production, graphic design, and web development, students learn the fundamentals of modern journalism and news production in written, audio, video and interactive formats. Students can specialize in news, sports, or digital journalism, or combine interests in a broader curriculum. Our curriculum trains you to ethically gather, analyze, and present information to a diverse public. Journalism students learn to use cutting-edge technology to report on news and create content for various platforms, including print, broadcast, and online publications. Graduates are prepared for careers in a dynamic and evolving media landscape.

The Legal Studies minor provides students from any major with a basic understanding of the American legal system. Students will develop foundational knowledge and skills in legal research, analysis, and writing that are applicable to a variety of careers in law, government, public service, and business. This minor will also provide a strong background for students considering law school or other graduate studies in law or public policy.

ProgramName: Associate of Arts in Liberal Arts -
Requirements: Complete and submit one of the following: Sacred Heart University Application or Common Application. Submit official high school transcript(s). Submit a guidance counselor recommendation. Submit an essay. Optional Items: ACT/SAT Test Scores (Sacred Heart University is a test-optional institution). Optional Items: Interview.
Description: The Associate of Arts in Liberal Arts prepares students for careers in fields that require critical thinking, strong communication skills, and a broad understanding of the world. This program emphasizes humanistic inquiry, scientific reasoning, and analytical skills, which are transferable to a wide variety of professions. The curriculum provides students with a foundational understanding of the arts, humanities, and social sciences, as well as a solid grounding in mathematics and natural sciences. Graduates will be well-prepared to pursue further education at the bachelor’s level or to enter the workforce directly. Sacred Heart University also offers a Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Arts, which provides a seamless transition for students wishing to continue their studies.
ScholarshipType: Academic Scholarships (Merit-based), Athletic Scholarships, Need-Based Aid, Performing Arts Scholarships, ROTC Scholarships, Brother/Sister and Legacy Scholarships

Requirements: Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application, Official High School Transcript, SAT/ACT Scores (optional for most programs), Letter of Recommendation (optional), Application Essay (optional), Counselor Report
Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
Description: With Sacred Heart University's Bachelor of Science in Marketing, you’ll learn what makes customers tick – how to reach them, how to understand their needs, and how to create campaigns that inspire action. Marketing is a fast-growing field and a crucial part of any business, whether it’s a non-profit organization or a Fortune 500 company. Our engaging, hands-on program focuses on the core principles of marketing and prepares you for success in today’s evolving job market. You'll gain a strong foundation in marketing fundamentals, including consumer behavior, market research, advertising, social media marketing, and digital marketing strategies. You will learn to analyze market trends, develop effective marketing plans, and utilize digital tools to reach target audiences. Through a blend of theoretical knowledge and practical experience, you’ll develop critical thinking, communication, and problem-solving skills that are essential for a successful career in marketing. Our dedicated faculty, with extensive industry experience, provide personalized mentorship and guidance, ensuring you receive the support you need to thrive. Beyond the classroom, you’ll have opportunities to participate in internships, student organizations, and real-world projects, giving you a competitive edge in the job market.
Accredidation: AACSB International – the premier global accrediting body for business schools.

Requirements: Students may declare a minor after they have earned 30 credits and are in good academic standing (2.0 cumulative GPA). A minor must be declared prior to filing a graduation application. A student may not declare a minor in the same discipline as his or her major unless the minor courses are distinct from the major.
Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
Description: Marketing has become a vital component of every organization's strategy. By taking a marketing minor, you will learn the fundamental skills needed to understand how to build brands, attract and retain customers, deliver value, and foster loyalty. The Marketing Minor is available to all students except those majoring in Marketing. It is a perfect complement to many majors, including Business Economics, Finance, Graphic Design, Communication and Media Arts, Sport Management, Psychology, Health Science, and more. To earn a minor in marketing, students must take a total of 18 credits (six courses) in marketing, including MKT 205 (Introduction to Marketing) and five additional 3-credit marketing courses. Students will work with their academic advisor to ensure that their marketing minor courses fit into their overall academic plan and align with their interests.

Requirements:
Complete the Common Application or SHU Application
Official high school transcript(s)
Counselor recommendation letter or school report
One letter of recommendation from a teacher
SAT and/or ACT scores (Sacred Heart University is test-optional for most undergraduate programs. If you choose not to submit test scores, you will not be at a disadvantage in the application or scholarship review process. If you decide not to submit your test scores, you will be required to submit a personal essay and your official high school transcript for evaluation. For students who choose to submit test scores, the average accepted SAT range is 1140-1250 and the average accepted ACT range is 23-28. For students applying to our Direct Entry Nursing program or other competitive health programs, the submission of test scores is highly encouraged, but not required.)
Personal essay (required if not submitting test scores)
Non-refundable $50 application fee or fee waiver
Description: Mathematics is the foundation for all scientific and technological advances. The Bachelor of Science in mathematics provides students with a strong foundation in core mathematics subjects such as calculus, linear algebra, discrete mathematics, and differential equations, along with advanced courses in topics such as abstract algebra, real analysis, probability and statistics. Students completing the BS in mathematics will possess critical thinking skills, problem-solving skills, and quantitative and analytical reasoning skills needed to thrive in a wide variety of careers or in graduate study.

A minor in mathematics provides a strong foundation in a field that supports many STEM disciplines. Mathematics plays an essential role in understanding and explaining the world around us and has applications in business, biology, computer science, and engineering.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Media Arts -
Requirements: Students interested in applying to Sacred Heart University as a first-year student must submit: Online Application (Common App or SHU Application), Official High School Transcript. Optional items include: Official SAT or ACT Scores (optional for all majors), Recommendation Letter (optional), Application Essay (optional).
Description: The Sacred Heart University Media Arts program is an interdisciplinary Bachelor of Arts program that offers students foundational skills and knowledge in audio, video, animation, graphic design and emerging media. By combining art and technology, students learn to critically analyze and creatively produce media in a variety of forms and platforms. The Media Arts program provides students with opportunities for research and creative expression through diverse projects that prepare them for a future in media. The program also provides an excellent foundation for graduate study. Graduates are prepared for careers in fields such as film, television, game design, digital marketing, animation, web design, podcasting, social media content creation, and multimedia production.
ScholarshipAmount: Academic Scholarships range from $15,000 to $27,000 per year.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Service, Performance, Athletics, Transfer, External, Endowed

Description: Sacred Heart University’s Middle Eastern Studies minor enables students to study the Middle East and North Africa from multiple disciplinary perspectives. This interdisciplinary minor allows students to apply the tools of political science, history, geography, economics, sociology, and religious studies to the study of the Middle East and North Africa as a region. The minor explores the region’s politics, culture, history, religions, and contemporary issues. It also examines the relationships of these countries to the rest of the world and their changing role in the international system. The Middle Eastern Studies minor is a multidisciplinary program drawing on courses in Arabic, economics, history, political science, and religious studies. It provides students with an integrated understanding of this strategically and culturally vital region of the world.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Athletic, Performing Arts, Phi Theta Kappa, Catholic High School, ROTC

Requirements: Currently enrolled Sacred Heart University students who have an interest in participating in the Army ROTC program may declare a Military Science minor. If you are not a current SHU student, you must apply to Sacred Heart University first and be accepted. Once you are accepted into SHU, you may then participate in the Army ROTC program. The Military Science minor has no specific GPA requirements outside of the general Sacred Heart University GPA requirements. Students must maintain a 2.0 GPA to remain in good standing with the university. If you are already enrolled in the Army ROTC program, you are eligible to declare a Military Science minor at any time.
Description: The Military Science minor offers students the opportunity to complement their academic major with an interdisciplinary program that includes topics related to leadership, military history, ethics, and national security. The minor is offered in collaboration with the Sacred Heart University Army Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC) program. This program is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of military leadership and operations, and to prepare them for potential careers in the U.S. Army. Students in the minor will learn to develop critical thinking skills, problem-solving abilities, and an understanding of organizational leadership within a military context. The minor includes courses in military history, strategic studies, and leadership development, providing a comprehensive overview of the military profession.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Molecular & Cellular Biology -
Requirements: Admission to Sacred Heart University for first-year students is based on several factors, including academic preparation, performance, and standardized test scores (if submitted). Sacred Heart is test-optional and does not require SAT or ACT scores. The University considers the academic success of students within the context of their high school curriculum and involvement in extracurricular activities through a holistic review process. Required materials include an official high school transcript and one letter of recommendation (preferably from your high school counselor). A personal essay is optional, but encouraged. Applicants can apply via the Common Application or the SHU Application.
Description: Molecular & Cellular Biology delves into the fundamental mechanisms of life at its most intricate levels, from DNA replication and protein synthesis to cellular communication and tissue development. Students in this program will learn to use cutting-edge technologies to answer fundamental biological questions about health and disease. This program provides students with the critical thinking, research, and communication skills necessary for careers in various fields, including medicine, research, biotechnology, pharmacology, and education. Our faculty are active researchers, publishing in peer-reviewed journals and presenting at national and international conferences, ensuring students are taught the most up-to-date concepts and techniques in the field. Students are strongly encouraged to participate in faculty-mentored research, either during the academic year or as part of our Summer Undergraduate Research Program (SURP). Students also have the opportunity to participate in internships in academic, medical, and industrial laboratories.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Diocesan, Athletic, Performing Arts, Need-based

Requirements:
To complete your application, please submit the following:
* Completed Common Application or Sacred Heart Application
* Official high school transcript
* Guidance counselor recommendation (optional)
* Official SAT/ACT scores (optional – Sacred Heart is test-optional)
* Personal essay (optional for students with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher; required for students with a GPA lower than 3.0)
* College credits (if applicable)
* Interviews (recommended for students with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher; required for students with a GPA lower than 3.0)
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Music at Sacred Heart University offers a comprehensive, interdisciplinary approach to the study of music as a human endeavor. Students delve into the historical, theoretical, cultural, and practical dimensions of music, fostering a deep understanding and appreciation for its diverse forms and functions. With a strong emphasis on critical thinking, creative expression, and collaborative learning, the program prepares students for a wide range of career paths in music, arts management, education, and related fields, or for further graduate study. Sacred Heart University's location in Fairfield County, Connecticut, provides unique opportunities for students to engage with a vibrant arts community, attend professional performances, and participate in internships with local music organizations. The program aims to cultivate well-rounded musicians and scholars who are not only technically proficient but also articulate, analytical, and socially conscious.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Performance-based (Music), Family Grants, Legacy Grants, Pioneer Grants, Diocesan Scholarships

Description: The Sacred Heart University Music Minor provides students with the opportunity to explore a variety of musical traditions and disciplines through performance, theory, history, and cultural studies. Students develop skills in critical listening, creative expression, and analytical thinking while engaging with diverse musical repertoires and styles. The minor is flexible, allowing students to tailor their studies to their interests, whether in classical, jazz, popular, world music, or other areas. It complements a wide range of majors, enhancing cultural literacy and fostering a lifelong appreciation for music.

Requirements: A completed online application (via the Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application), Official high school transcript(s), Two letters of recommendation (one from a school counselor and one from a teacher), Personal essay, Official college transcripts (if applicable).
Description: Are you fascinated by the complexity of the brain and how it impacts behavior? Neuroscience is an interdisciplinary field that examines the nervous system, focusing on its structure, function, development, and pathology. Neuroscience majors at SHU gain a comprehensive understanding of the brain and nervous system, integrating knowledge from biology, chemistry, psychology, and computer science. You will explore topics such as neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, neuropharmacology, cognitive neuroscience, and behavioral neuroscience. This program is designed to provide a strong foundation for various careers in scientific research, healthcare, education, and biotechnology.

Requirements: Official High School Transcripts with an overall B average (3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale), Essay/Personal Statement, One letter of recommendation (guidance counselor or teacher), Official SAT or ACT Scores (optional for applicants with a 3.0 or higher cumulative GPA). Please note: For Nursing, Math (Algebra I & II and Geometry) and Science (Chemistry and Biology) are required. Physics is recommended but not required.
Description: Sacred Heart University’s Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) prepares you for a successful career in today’s evolving health care environment. As one of the largest nursing programs in Connecticut, we prepare students to be leaders in the field. Our program offers many opportunities to collaborate and innovate in interdisciplinary teams. Our student nurses gain valuable hands-on experience through clinical placements, service-learning and international experiences, state-of-the-art simulation labs, research projects with faculty, and student leadership opportunities. With a low faculty-to-student ratio, we provide a personalized education in a supportive learning environment. We are focused on cultivating the critical thinking and clinical skills necessary to provide evidence-based, patient-centered care. Graduates are prepared for a variety of nursing roles and are eligible to sit for the National Council Licensure Examination (NCLEX-RN).
Accredidation: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education, 655 K Street NW, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001, 202-887-6791. Sacred Heart University's School of Nursing is also accredited by the Connecticut State Board of Examiners for Nursing.

Requirements:
Academic Requirements for Freshmen Applicants: Students must have a cumulative high school GPA of 3.0 or higher. Students must have completed 4 units of English, 3 units of Math (Algebra I & II and Geometry), 3 units of Science (Biology, Chemistry, and Physics), and 4 units of Social Studies. Students must have achieved an average GPA of 3.0 in Math and Science coursework.
Academic Requirements for Transfer Applicants: Students must have a cumulative college GPA of 3.0 or higher. Students must have completed 4 units of English, 3 units of Math (Algebra I & II and Geometry), 3 units of Science (Biology, Chemistry, and Physics), and 4 units of Social Studies at the high school level OR completed college equivalents. Students must have achieved an average GPA of 3.0 in Math and Science coursework at the high school or college level.
How to Apply - First-year applicants to the Occupational Therapy BS/MOT program must apply through the Common Application. Required materials for first-year applicants: Common Application, Official high school transcript, Optional: SAT/ACT scores, Letters of recommendation (optional), Essay (optional).
How to Apply - Transfer applicants must apply through the Sacred Heart University application for admission. Required materials for transfer applicants: Sacred Heart University application for admission, Official high school transcript, Official college transcripts, Essay (optional), Letters of recommendation (optional).
Description: Occupational Therapy (OT) is a health and rehabilitation profession focused on helping people across the lifespan participate in the things they want and need to do through the therapeutic use of everyday activities (occupations). Common occupational therapy interventions include helping children with disabilities to participate fully in school and social situations, helping people recovering from injury to regain skills, and providing support for older adults experiencing physical and cognitive changes. Sacred Heart University's Occupational Therapy Program offers a combined Bachelor of Science in Health Science and Master of Science in Occupational Therapy (BS/MOT) program for high school students interested in a career in occupational therapy. This accelerated program takes five years to complete compared to the typical six years. Students are admitted to the professional phase of the program after successfully completing the first three years of undergraduate coursework with the required academic average and specific pre-requisite courses. The professional phase consists of two years of graduate coursework and fieldwork. Students completing the program are eligible to sit for the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) examination to become a Registered Occupational Therapist (OTR).
Accredidation: The Occupational Therapy Program at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education (ACOTE) of the American Occupational Therapy Association (AOTA), located at 6116 Executive Boulevard, Suite 200, North Bethesda, MD 20852-4929. ACOTE’s telephone number c/o AOTA is (301) 652-AOTA and its Web address is www.acoteonline.org.

Description:
Welcome to the Sacred Heart University Philosophy Department, where we invite you to embark on a profound journey of critical thinking, ethical inquiry, and intellectual exploration. Our department is dedicated to fostering a vibrant academic community where students engage with fundamental questions about existence, knowledge, values, and the human condition.
Whether you choose to pursue a major or a minor in Philosophy, you will develop invaluable skills in logical reasoning, analytical thinking, and effective communication. Our curriculum is designed to challenge your assumptions, broaden your perspectives, and equip you with the intellectual tools necessary to navigate an increasingly complex world.
At Sacred Heart University, philosophy is not merely an academic discipline; it is a way of life—a commitment to thoughtful inquiry, ethical action, and the pursuit of wisdom. Join us as we explore the rich history of philosophical thought, engage with contemporary issues, and cultivate the intellectual virtues that will empower you to make a meaningful difference in the world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy, Politics & Economics -
Requirements: Completed Application (Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application), Official High School Transcript, School Counselor Recommendation (strongly recommended), One Academic Teacher Recommendation (strongly recommended), Essay (strongly recommended for test-optional applicants), SAT or ACT scores (optional).
Description: The Sacred Heart University bachelor of arts in Philosophy, Politics & Economics (PPE) provides an interdisciplinary and integrative approach to understanding and addressing issues of social justice and economic welfare. Drawing on the disciplines of philosophy, political science, and economics, the PPE major emphasizes critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and evidence-based decision-making. Students develop a deep understanding of the foundations of political, economic, and social institutions and the complex interplay between them. The PPE major is highly customizable, allowing students to tailor their coursework to their specific interests and career goals. Students choose courses from each of the three disciplines, including options in moral philosophy, political theory, public policy, microeconomics, macroeconomics, and international economics. The program culminates in a capstone project that allows students to apply their interdisciplinary knowledge to a real-world problem or policy issue. Graduates of the PPE program are well-prepared for a wide range of careers in law, public service, business, and non-profit organizations, as well as for graduate study in related fields.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Athletic, Alumni & Friends, Performing Arts, ROTC, Diocesan

Description: Sacred Heart University’s accelerated BS/DPT program offers highly motivated students a direct path to a rewarding career as a doctor of physical therapy. This integrated six-year program combines foundational liberal arts and science courses with a comprehensive physical therapy curriculum, preparing you for advanced clinical practice. Our state-of-the-art facilities, extensive clinical partnerships, and dedicated faculty provide an immersive learning experience focused on evidence-based practice and patient-centered care. Graduates are well-prepared to excel in diverse healthcare settings and contribute meaningfully to the physical therapy profession.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Physical Therapy program at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE), 3030 Potomac Ave., Suite 100, Alexandria, Virginia 22305-3085; telephone: 703-706-3245; email: accreditation@apta.org; website: http://www.capteonline.org. If needing to contact the program/institution directly, please call 203-365-7634 or email pt@sacredheart.edu.

Requirements:
Required application materials for first-year applicants:
*   Online Application (Common Application or SHU Application)
*   Official High School Transcript
*   Letter of Recommendation (from a school counselor or teacher)
*   Essay/Personal Statement
Description: From studying gravity, forces, and motion to energy, sound, light, electricity, and magnetism, physics is the scientific field that examines how the universe works. If you are interested in exploring a career as a scientist, engineer, or educator, Sacred Heart University’s Bachelor of Science (BS) in physics program provides the solid foundational knowledge and hands-on laboratory experience you need to succeed. Our challenging program combines rigorous classroom instruction with extensive practical experience in our state-of-the-art physics labs. You will learn to think critically, solve problems, analyze data, and communicate effectively—skills that are highly valued in any profession. Physics majors at SHU gain a comprehensive understanding of the physical world and develop valuable analytical skills that are applicable in a wide range of careers. The physics program culminates in a senior capstone research project where you will apply your knowledge to solve real-world problems. This project provides an opportunity to delve deeper into a specific area of physics that interests you and to showcase your research skills.
ScholarshipType: Merit-Based, Athletic, Performance, Need-Based, Other Grants

Description: Physics is a foundational science, integral to understanding the fundamental nature of the universe. In this program, you will develop problem-solving skills, critical thinking, and a deep appreciation for the scientific method. At SHU, we emphasize hands-on learning, encouraging students to engage in research and apply theoretical knowledge to real-world scenarios. Our faculty are dedicated mentors, guiding students through challenging coursework and fostering a collaborative learning environment. Whether you aspire to contribute to scientific research, innovative technology, or advanced studies, a Physics degree from SHU equips you with the analytical and technical skills essential for success.
ScholarshipType: Academic-based, Athletic, Fine Arts, Transfer Student, Alumni, Endowed, Outside Scholarships

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science -
Requirements: Common Application or SHU Online Application, Official High School Transcript(s), Recommendation from a Counselor or Teacher, Essay, SAT/ACT (Optional for most programs), Official College Transcript(s) (if applicable)
Concentration: American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory, public law and public policy, global studies
Description: The study of political science helps students develop a critical understanding of political systems, institutions, processes, and policies. It encourages students to think broadly about politics, power, and society, as well as the important questions of justice, equality, and freedom. The Political Science curriculum offers a comprehensive education in American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory, public law, and public policy, as well as global studies. The program is designed to develop students’ analytical, research, and communication skills, which are essential for success in a wide range of careers and graduate programs. Specializations within the Political Science major include American politics, comparative politics, international relations, political theory, public law and public policy, and global studies. The major emphasizes critical thinking, close reading, rigorous writing, and oral communication. The curriculum also promotes engagement in co-curricular activities and public service. A Political Science major teaches students how to be active and responsible citizens in a democratic society and a global community.

Requirements: Common Application or SHU Application, Official high school transcript(s), One letter of recommendation from a school counselor or teacher, Essay/personal statement (prompt available on Common App), Optional: SAT or ACT scores, Optional: Resume
Description: Sacred Heart University’s Bachelor of Arts in Psychology is designed to provide a broad understanding of the field and prepare students for a variety of careers or graduate study. The program emphasizes critical thinking, research methods, and ethical practice. Students explore topics such as human development, social psychology, cognitive processes, abnormal psychology, and neuroscience. The curriculum offers a balance of theoretical knowledge and practical experience, including opportunities for internships, research projects, and community engagement.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Honors Program, Alumni & Family, Performing Arts, Athletic, ROTC

Description: The minor in psychology is available to all Sacred Heart University students. It requires 18 credits in psychology, of which nine credits must be at the 200-level or above. Students must take PS 101: Introduction to Psychology. For their remaining five courses (15 credits), students may choose any psychology courses. The minor allows students to broaden their knowledge in the discipline of psychology to complement their chosen major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Health -
Requirements: First-year applicants can apply through the Common Application or the Sacred Heart University Application. There is no application fee. Application Checklist: Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application, Official High School Transcript(s), Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, Academic Essay/Personal Statement (required for some programs).
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Public Health is designed to prepare students to advance public health through a variety of careers in both clinical and community settings. Students will explore and develop an understanding of epidemiology, social and behavioral health, environmental health, and health policy and management. Graduates will develop skills in the core competencies of public health by focusing on population health across the lifespan, health education and promotion, and the prevention of disease and injury. The Public Health BS program at Sacred Heart University emphasizes hands-on learning, community engagement, and critical thinking to address complex public health challenges.

ProgramName: RN to Bachelor of Science in Nursing - BSN
Requirements:
Active, unencumbered RN license (must maintain licensure throughout the program)
Associate degree or diploma from an accredited nursing program
Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5
Successful completion of a basic statistics course
An official transcript from each college and university attended
Current resume/CV
Online application
Description: The RN to Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) program at Sacred Heart University is designed specifically for registered nurses who wish to advance their education and career. This program offers a flexible and convenient pathway for RNs to earn a bachelor’s degree in nursing, enhancing their professional knowledge, leadership skills, and career opportunities. Through a comprehensive curriculum, students will deepen their understanding of evidence-based practice, healthcare policy, community health, and nursing leadership. The program emphasizes critical thinking, ethical decision-making, and cultural competency, preparing graduates to provide high-quality, patient-centered care in diverse healthcare settings. Sacred Heart University’s RN to BSN program is ideal for working nurses, offering both online and hybrid course options to accommodate busy schedules. Graduates are prepared for advanced roles in clinical practice, education, administration, and public health, contributing to improved patient outcomes and the advancement of the nursing profession.
Accredidation: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing at Sacred Heart University is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE), 655 K Street, NW, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001, 202-887-6791.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Social Work -
Requirements: Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application, Official high school transcripts, Guidance counselor recommendation, Personal essay, Official SAT/ACT test scores (optional for most programs), Official college transcripts (if applicable). Sacred Heart University has a Test-Optional policy for applicants who wish to be reviewed without submitting SAT or ACT scores.
Department: Isabelle Farrington College of Education & Human Development
Description: The Sacred Heart University Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Social Work prepares you to become a generalist social worker. Graduates are trained to work with individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities within diverse practice settings. We prepare our graduates to work with the most vulnerable populations who are facing a multitude of issues across the lifespan. Through our curriculum, you will develop the knowledge, values, and skills to provide ethical, anti-racist, and trauma-informed social work services. Our goal is to promote social and economic justice while working to alleviate poverty and oppression. The BA in Social Work prepares students for either employment at the baccalaureate level or graduate education for advanced practice.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE) Commission on Accreditation.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Alumni, Sibling, Athletic, Music, eSports, ROTC

Requirements: We require the following materials from first-year applicants: Official High School Transcript(s), Counselor Recommendation, One Academic Teacher Recommendation, Application essay
Description: Sociology is the scientific study of human society, social behavior, and social structure. It examines how social forces and institutions influence individuals and groups, as well as how individuals and groups shape society. Sociologists explore various topics, including social inequality, race and ethnicity, gender, family, crime, education, religion, and globalization. Through rigorous research methods and theoretical frameworks, sociologists strive to understand the complexities of social life, analyze social problems, and contribute to positive social change. Our department offers a Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in sociology. Our BS in sociology offers you a comprehensive understanding of human behavior and societal structures. The program is specifically designed to provide you with the theoretical knowledge and research skills necessary to analyze complex social issues and contribute to positive social change. With a strong emphasis on research methods and statistical analysis, you will develop a deep understanding of social phenomena and their impact on individuals and communities. Sociology graduates are well-prepared for a variety of careers in social work, public administration, education, market research, urban planning, law enforcement, and more. The analytical, research, and communication skills acquired through a sociology degree are highly valued in diverse professional settings. Additionally, the BS in sociology provides an excellent foundation for graduate studies in sociology, social work, law, and other related fields.

Requirements: Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application, Official High School Transcript(s), SAT/ACT (optional), Essay/Personal Statement, Letter of Recommendation, School Report
Description: The Spanish major focuses on an in-depth study of the Spanish language and its literature. This program prepares students for a career in education or graduate study, and it pairs well with other majors or minors. You will enhance your understanding of Hispanic culture through the study of authors and texts from Spain, Latin America and the United States. The Spanish major offers a well-rounded curriculum in Spanish language, literature, culture, linguistics, and civilization. Our students gain fluency and proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing, and they develop a comprehensive knowledge of the diverse cultures of the Spanish-speaking world.

Whether you plan to continue your studies or work in your chosen field, adding a minor in Spanish will enhance your career opportunities. Being fluent in Spanish and having an understanding of Hispanic cultures will open doors to new career paths both domestically and abroad. Our Spanish minor provides students with competency in the language and a broad understanding of the Spanish and Latin American cultures, as well as opportunities for cultural enrichment through a range of experiences from community engagement to study abroad. Students who major in Spanish may not minor in Spanish.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Speech-Language Pathology -
Requirements: A complete application submitted online through the Common Application or the SHU Online Application. An official high school transcript. A letter of recommendation from your school counselor or a teacher. Test scores (optional) – Official SAT or ACT scores. Sacred Heart University is test-optional for most undergraduate programs. If you choose to submit your scores, you can self-report them at the time of application or send official scores directly from the College Board (SAT code 3779) or ACT (code 0601). Sacred Heart will consider your highest scores. A personal statement/essay (optional) – This is the same personal statement/essay you would submit via Common App. An interview (optional) – An interview can provide the Admissions Committee with more information about you and provide you with an opportunity to learn more about Sacred Heart. Interviews are offered both virtually and in-person. A portfolio/audition (optional) – Required for some programs, such as art & design, digital marketing, and music.
Description: Speech-language pathology is a rewarding profession where you can make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals with communication disorders. As a speech-language pathologist, you will diagnose and treat a wide range of speech, language, cognitive, voice, and swallowing disorders across the lifespan. You'll work with diverse populations in various settings, including schools, hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and private practices. Sacred Heart University's Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Speech-Language Pathology program provides a comprehensive and rigorous curriculum designed to prepare students for graduate studies and a successful career in the field. Our program emphasizes evidence-based practices, clinical reasoning, and interprofessional collaboration. Students gain a strong foundation in communication sciences and disorders, develop critical thinking skills, and learn to apply their knowledge in real-world settings. With dedicated faculty, state-of-the-art facilities, and diverse clinical experiences, we are committed to fostering compassionate and competent speech-language pathologists who are prepared to meet the communication needs of individuals and communities.
Accredidation: Sacred Heart University’s Speech-Language Pathology Program, Bachelor of Science (BS) is an accredited program recognized by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA). This accreditation signifies that our program meets rigorous academic and professional standards, ensuring that our graduates are well-prepared for entry-level practice and further graduate studies. The CAA's accreditation is a testament to the quality and excellence of our curriculum, faculty, and clinical education experiences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sport Management -
Requirements: The following items must be submitted to complete your application: Completed application (Common Application or SHU Application), Official high school transcript, Official SAT/ACT scores (Optional for students with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher), Essay (Personal Statement), Letter of Recommendation (from a counselor or teacher). While we don’t have a minimum GPA or test score requirement, most of our applicants have a B average (3.0 on a 4.0 scale) and competitive SAT/ACT scores. We recommend that you complete a college preparatory curriculum in high school, including: 4 years of English, 3-4 years of math (Algebra I & II, Geometry, Pre-Calculus), 3-4 years of science (Biology, Chemistry, Physics), 3-4 years of social science, 2-3 years of foreign language.
Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
Description: The world of sports is complex and diverse, requiring professionals with a wide range of skills to manage various aspects such as marketing, finance, operations, and human resources. Sacred Heart University’s Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Sport Management program prepares you for a rewarding career in this dynamic field. Our curriculum combines business principles with sport-specific knowledge, providing you with a solid foundation in both areas. You'll gain a deep understanding of the unique challenges and opportunities within the sport industry, from amateur to professional levels. Through a blend of classroom learning, experiential opportunities, and industry connections, you'll develop the practical skills and theoretical knowledge needed to succeed. Our faculty, composed of experienced professionals and scholars, are dedicated to providing a supportive and engaging learning environment. Whether you aspire to work in professional sports, collegiate athletics, event management, or sport marketing, our program equips you with the tools to achieve your goals. Join us and turn your passion for sports into a successful career.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sports Communication & Media -
Requirements: A completed Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application; Official high school transcript(s); Official SAT or ACT scores (optional for most programs, except nursing); Letter of Recommendation (optional); Essay (optional - included in Common App); Application fee.
Department: School of Communication, Media & the Arts
Description: The Sports Communication & Media major provides a comprehensive understanding of the communication and media aspects of the sports industry. Students learn about sports journalism, broadcasting, public relations, social media, and marketing within a sports context. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience through internships, campus media organizations, and real-world projects. Students will develop strong writing, speaking, and digital media production skills, essential for success in today’s evolving media landscape. Core courses cover topics such as sports reporting, media law and ethics, sports broadcasting production, public relations in sports, and digital sports content creation. The program also allows for elective courses in areas of interest, providing flexibility for students to tailor their education to specific career goals.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Performing Arts, Transfer Student, Veterans Benefits

Department: Jack Welch College of Business & Technology
Description: The Sports Management minor is an 18-credit program providing students with fundamental business, communication, and management skills necessary to succeed in the diverse sports industry. This minor is open to all Sacred Heart University students and can be paired with any major.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Performing Arts, Athletic, Alumni

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Strategic Communication, Public Relations & Advertising -
Requirements: Online application (Common App or SHU Application), Official high school transcript, SAT or ACT scores (optional), One letter of recommendation (from a teacher or school counselor), Personal essay, Early Decision applicants will need to submit a signed Early Decision Agreement Form. Portfolios for Art & Design, Dance, Music, Theatre Arts applicants are optional, but strongly encouraged.
Description:
Strategic Communication, Public Relations & Advertising is one of the most exciting, dynamic, and rapidly evolving fields in the country. Our program offers you the opportunity to learn how to communicate effectively, think critically and creatively, and apply those skills to various professional contexts, from public relations and advertising to corporate communications and social media. You will gain a solid foundation in communication theory and research, while also developing practical skills in writing, speaking, presenting, and problem-solving. This includes opportunities to:
*   Develop a portfolio of work to showcase your skills and talents
*   Gain real-world experience through internships and practicums
*   Network with professionals in the field
*   Learn from award-winning faculty with diverse backgrounds and expertise
*   Travel to national communication conferences

The curriculum combines theory with hands-on practice, preparing you for a variety of careers in both the private and public sectors. You will explore topics such as media relations, crisis communication, social media strategy, advertising campaigns, and intercultural communication. With a focus on ethical and socially responsible communication, our program emphasizes the importance of diversity, inclusion, and global perspectives in today’s interconnected world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theatre Arts -
Requirements: Completed Common Application or Sacred Heart University Application, Official high school transcript, Official standardized test scores (SAT and/or ACT) - Sacred Heart University is a test-optional institution, Counselor letter of recommendation, Official college transcripts (if applicable). No additional supplemental requirements for Theatre Arts (BA).
Description: Sacred Heart’s Theatre Arts BA program challenges students to hone their skills as performers, designers, technicians, stage managers, directors, producers, and educators. This program provides students with a strong foundation in all areas of theatre through coursework that emphasizes collaboration, creativity, critical thinking, and communication skills. A Theatre Arts major will develop a comprehensive understanding of dramatic literature, theatre history, and contemporary theatre practices.
