Students also learn how to create and produce theatrical performances, from concept to curtain. Our faculty are experts in their fields, bringing a wealth of professional experience to the classroom. They are dedicated to helping students achieve their artistic and academic goals.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Performance, Athletic, ROTC, Endowed & Restricted, Diocesan, Pioneer Spotlight Award

Requirements: Sacred Heart University accepts the Sacred Heart University Application or Common Application. In addition to the online application, applicants should submit the following: Official High School Transcripts (submitted directly from your high school), Official College Transcripts (if applicable), Letter of Recommendation from a school counselor or teacher (optional). Sacred Heart University is a test-optional institution. While not required, applicants may submit official SAT or ACT scores.
Description: A Theatre Arts minor helps students enhance their acting, directing, design, and technical skills while providing a deeper understanding of the history and theory of theatre. Students are immersed in creating, experiencing, and studying theatre both inside and outside the classroom. They have the opportunity to participate in main stage productions through the Department of Theatre Arts Program, student-run productions through TheatreFest, and various workshops. Theatre arts minors develop valuable skills in critical thinking, public speaking, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Athletic, Performing Arts, Catholic High School, Community Awareness, First Generation, Transfer, Honors Program

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theology & Religious Studies -
Requirements: A completed Common Application or SHU Application; Official high school transcripts; SAT or ACT scores (optional, but encouraged for scholarship consideration); One letter of recommendation (preferably from a school counselor or teacher); Optional: essay, resume, additional letters of recommendation, and/or portfolio
Description: The undergraduate major in Theology and Religious Studies introduces students to the academic study of religion as a human phenomenon. It seeks to understand religion's diverse expressions (beliefs, texts, ethics, rituals, institutions, communities, and experiences) in various historical and cultural contexts, paying particular attention to the Christian tradition and its Catholic expression. Students gain an understanding of religion's influence on societies and individuals globally and domestically, along with an appreciation for religious diversity in the world today. The program aims to develop religiously literate citizens of the world, capable of critical inquiry and constructive engagement with religious traditions and issues related to religion and society. A student majoring in Theology and Religious Studies will engage in historical, textual, theological, and ethical inquiry, and learn to apply theoretical and methodological tools for understanding religion. The Theology and Religious Studies program offers an excellent foundation for graduate studies and professions in education, law, social work, journalism, public service, and ministry.
ScholarshipType: Academic, Performing Arts, Athletic, Community Service, Alumni

Description: A minor in Theology and Religious Studies provides students with the opportunity to explore profound questions concerning religious traditions, practices, and beliefs. Theology and Religious Studies minors foster critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and cultural understanding, preparing students to engage with diverse perspectives and make informed decisions in an increasingly complex world. Students with a minor in Theology and Religious Studies are well-equipped to contribute to professions that require cultural competence and ethical deliberation, such as education, social work, law, healthcare, journalism, and ministry.

Requirements: A complete application for undergraduate admission includes: Official high school transcript, One letter of recommendation (preferably from a school counselor or teacher). Official SAT or ACT scores are optional for most programs.
Description: The Web Design & Development minor at Sacred Heart University is designed for students interested in learning the fundamental principles and techniques of creating and maintaining dynamic websites. This minor provides a blend of design aesthetics, user experience (UX) principles, and technical development skills, preparing students to build engaging and functional web solutions. Students will explore front-end development (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), back-end basics, content management systems (CMS), and responsive design, equipping them with a comprehensive skill set for the digital age. This minor is suitable for students from various disciplines who wish to enhance their digital literacy and career prospects in web-related fields.

The Women, Gender and Sexuality Studies minor provides an interdisciplinary lens through which students can analyze gendered power relations in society, politics, and culture. The minor examines gender as a social construct, intersecting with race, class, sexuality, ability, and religion to shape human experience. Students will develop critical thinking skills necessary to analyze historical and contemporary understandings of gender and sexuality and their impact on individuals and communities. Students will be exposed to feminist theory, gender theory, and queer theory, and will learn how these frameworks are used to analyze various topics such as masculinity, globalization, human rights, and social justice. The WGSS minor will provide students with marketable skills that complement majors across the university. The minor will prepare students for a range of careers in fields such as social work, public policy, non-profit organizations, education, journalism, and advocacy, among others. Students will be encouraged to explore opportunities for community engagement and internships in gender and sexuality-related organizations.
